definition_zh: 恶名；臭名；声名狼藉；坏名声
definition_en: the state of being famous for something bad
core_image: 街头小报的头版上印着一张脸，人人都认得，却没人敢向他问好
scene: 那几年他的照片频频登上八卦小报的头版，走到哪里都有人侧目。The failed banker soon gained international notoriety after his fund collapsed overnight.
sceneCN: 这里 notoriety 是「恶名、声名狼藉」（第 1 个义项：因坏事而出名）；句意：那家基金一夜之间垮掉之后，这位失败的投资银行家很快在国际上声名狼藉。

pos.zh: 因某件事而广为人知（常指坏事）

collocations.zh: 声名狼藉（书面强化的说法）

derivatives.zh: 由 notoriety 的词干加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「臭名昭著的」
notorious 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「众所周知地（常带贬义）」
notorious 加 -ness 构成的抽象名词，义为「恶名昭彰的性质」，少见

senses.title: Fame for something bad
senses.definition: the state of being widely known for something wrong, shameful, or criminal
senses.definitionCN: 因做错事、丑事或犯罪而被众人熟知的状态
senses.example: The firm gained notoriety after the scandal broke.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻曝光后，这家公司声名狼藉。
senses.why: The Latin source notorius means well known, so what spread first was simply news; the bad colour came later, when only crimes made good headlines.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 notorius 意为「被人熟知的」，所以这个词最初只表示消息传开；后来只有罪行才上得了头条，贬义才随之而来。

senses.title: Publicly known fact
senses.titleCN: 众所周知的事实；公开的知名度
senses.definition: the quality of being publicly known or openly acknowledged by everyone
senses.definitionCN: 被公众知道、被众人公开承认的性质
senses.example: In law, notoriety of a fact may excuse the need for proof.
senses.exampleCN: 在法律上，某一事实若众所周知，就可能无须再举证。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: anything openly known has notoriety, long before anyone judged it good or bad.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层含义：只要事情公开为人所知，就有 notoriety，那时人们还没评判它好坏。

senses.title: A person with a bad name
senses.titleCN: 声名狼藉的人；有名的坏家伙
senses.definition: a person who is widely known, usually because of wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 广为人知的人，通常因为做过坏事而知名
senses.example: The old saloon was full of local notorieties.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老酒馆里坐满了当地声名狼藉的人物。
senses.why: The abstract noun can be counted, so notoriety also names the person who carries the bad name.
senses.whyCN: 这个抽象名词可以计数，所以 notoriety 也能直接从「坏名声」转指背着坏名声的那个人。

senses.title: Bad repute of a place
senses.definition: the poor reputation that a place, street, or institution has among people
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、街道或机构在人们中间的坏名声
senses.example: The area earned notoriety as a smuggling port.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带因走私港口而出了名。
senses.why: Once bad fame belongs to a person, it easily moves to any place where such people gather, so notoriety attaches to streets, towns, and companies.
senses.whyCN: 坏名声先属于个人，然后很容易转移到这类人聚集的地方，所以 notoriety 也会落到街道、城镇和公司头上。

senses.title: A notorious act or case
senses.titleCN: 臭名昭著的案件；恶名事件
senses.definition: a specific deed or court case that is widely and unfavourably known
senses.definitionCN: 被广泛而负面地知晓的具体行为或案件
senses.example: The judge mentioned the notoriety of the earlier case.
senses.exampleCN: 法官提到了早先那桩案件臭名昭著的性质。
senses.why: A single act can become so widely talked about that the word names the deed itself, not just the fame of it.
senses.whyCN: 单独一件事也可能被议论得足够广，于是这个词不仅指名声，还直接指那件事本身。

senses.title: Fame through oddity
senses.titleCN: 因古怪而出名；奇闻带来的名声
senses.definition: wide public recognition gained through strange behaviour or eccentric appeal rather than crime
senses.definitionCN: 因古怪行为或奇特魅力而非罪行获得的广泛关注
senses.example: The small cafe won a gentle notoriety for its upside-down menu.
senses.exampleCN: 那家小咖啡馆因菜单上下颠倒而小有名气。
senses.why: If being known is the core and badness only the usual companion, fame won by odd behaviour can still borrow the word with a smile.
senses.whyCN: 如果「为人所知」是核心、「坏」只是常见伴随，那么靠古怪行为换来的出名也可以用这个词，只是带点玩笑意味。

senses.title: Open knowledge in law
senses.titleCN: 法律上的公开性；众所周知性
senses.definition: in legal usage, the open and universal quality of something that needs no proof
senses.definitionCN: 法律用语中，某事物不证自明的公开普遍性质
senses.example: The court relied on the notoriety of the established practice.
senses.exampleCN: 法院依据这一惯例的众所周知性作出判断。
senses.why: Law keeps the oldest neutral duty of the word: what everyone openly knows carries its own proof.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了这个词最古老的中立含义：人人都公开知道的事情，本身就能作证。

senses.title: Negative note in fame words
senses.definition: the shade of disapproval that separates being famous from being widely known for something bad
senses.definitionCN: 把「有名」与「因坏事出名」区分开来的那层不赞成色彩
senses.example: The name had fame, but his had notoriety instead.
senses.exampleCN: 那个名字拥有的是美名，而他的则是恶名。
senses.why: Fame and reputation are neutral, so over time notoriety became the word we reach for when the attention is unwelcome.
senses.whyCN: fame 和 reputation 都是中性的，久而久之 notoriety 就成了当关注令人不快时人们会选用的那个词。

intro.en: Notoriety comes from Latin notus, known, through notorius, well known; the bad sense was added in French and English usage.
intro.cn: notoriety 源自拉丁语 notus（已知的），经 notorius（广为人知的）而来；贬义是在法语与英语的使用中逐渐加上去的。

items.en: The verb noscere means to come to know, and its participle notus means known.
items.cn: 动词 noscere 意为「认识到」，其分词 notus 意为「已知的」。

items.en: The adjective notorius means well known, at first without any judgement of good or bad.
items.cn: 形容词 notorius 意为「广为人知的」，最初并不含褒贬判断。

items.en: Legal writing uses notorium for facts that are openly known and need no proof.
items.cn: 中世纪法律文书中用 notorium 指公开知晓、无须举证的事实。

items.en: French notoriété carries the abstract noun into everyday use.
items.cn: 法语 notoriété 把这个抽象名词带入日常使用。

items.en: English takes notoriety, first naming open public knowledge.
items.cn: 英语吸收 notoriety，起初指公开的知名事实。

items.en: The modern sense settles on fame won by wrongdoing, while law keeps the neutral reading.
items.cn: 现代义固定为因坏事获得的名声，而法律用语仍保留中立含义。

note.en: Notoriety is the noun of a name spread too far, close to the notorious family and to ordinary fame words.
note.cn: notoriety 是「名声传得太远」的名词，与 notorious 词族以及普通的「出名」词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Notoriety is a name that spread further than the person wanted.
normalIntro.cn: notoriety 是一个传播得比本人希望的更远的名字。

normal.en: Gain notoriety is the standard verb pair for earning a bad name.
normal.cn: gain notoriety 是表示「挣得坏名声」的标准动词搭配。

normal.en: One letter separates notorious from notoriety: the same bad name in adjective and noun form.
normal.cn: notorious 与 notoriety 只差一个字母，就是同一个坏名声的形容词与名词形式。

normal.en: Behind the word sits Latin notus, known, so notoriety is literally knownness.
normal.cn: 这个词背后是拉丁语 notus（已知的），所以 notoriety 字面上就是「被人知道」的状态。

normal.en: Use notoriety for people, streets, and scandals, but keep fame neutral.
normal.cn: notoriety 用于人、街道与丑闻，而 fame 保持中性。

normal.en: Compare infamy: infamy is darker and moral, notoriety is wider and cooler.
normal.cn: 对比 infamy：infamy 更阴暗、更具道德谴责，notoriety 更宽泛、语气更冷。

abstract.en: See a grainy newspaper photo of one face on every front page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张模糊的报纸照片，每份头版上都是同一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a town square notice board with one name pinned in every corner.
abstract.cn: 想象广场公告板的每个角落都钉着同一个名字。

abstract.en: Think of a whispered name that makes people look up and step back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被低声提起的名字，让人抬头并后退一步。

examples.en: The hotel gained notoriety for its rude service.
examples.cn: 那家酒店因服务粗暴而恶名远扬。

examples.en: Despite its notoriety, the street remains a busy market.
examples.cn: 尽管名声不佳，这条街仍是热闹的市场。

examples.en: He seemed to enjoy the notoriety his jokes brought him.
examples.cn: 他似乎很享受自己的笑话带来的那点坏名声。

root: 拉丁语 noscere（认识到）→ 分词 notus（已知的）→ notorius（广为人知的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 notorium（公开可知的事实）→ 法语 notoriété → 英语 notoriety，核心义「被人知道」。

sensesIntro.en: Notoriety begins as open public knowledge, then narrows into fame for wrongdoing, and finally reaches the people, places, and cases that wear that bad name.
sensesIntro.cn: notoriety 最初指公开的公众认知，随后收窄为因坏事而有的名声，最后扩展到背着坏名声的人、地方与案件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face everyone recognises and no one greets.
core.cn: 核心意象：人人都认得、却没人敢打招呼的那张脸。

branches.en: Fame for something bad is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 因坏事出名是占主导的现代义项。

branches.en: Open public knowledge is the oldest neutral sense.
branches.cn: 公开的公众认知是最古老的中立义项。

branches.en: The person who carries the bad name is the countable sense.
branches.cn: 背着坏名声的人是可计数的义项。

branches.en: Places and single cases inherit the bad name from people.
branches.cn: 地方与单个案件从人那里继承了坏名声。

branches.en: Oddity, legal openness, and fame words show how far the neutral core still reaches.
branches.cn: 古怪出名、法律公开性与「出名」类词语，显示出中立核心仍延伸多远。

senses.title: Famous for something bad
senses.definition: widely and unfavourably known because of wrong or harmful behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 因错误或有害的行为而被广泛负面地知晓
senses.example: The prison was notorious for its brutal guards.
senses.exampleCN: 那所监狱因看守残暴而臭名昭著。
senses.why: The Latin adjective notorius first meant simply well known; once bad deeds drew the crowd, the adjective kept only the bad side.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语形容词 notorius 最初只表示「广为人知」；当坏事最吸引围观之后，这个形容词只留下了坏的一面。

senses.title: Well known for a quality
senses.definition: well known for a particular quality, often an unflattering one
senses.definitionCN: 因某一特点而出了名，常是令人不悦的特点
senses.example: This city is notorious for its summer heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市以夏季酷热出了名。
senses.why: The badness can loosen to mere noticeable flaw, so a city, a road, or a menu can carry the same word.
senses.whyCN: 「坏」可以放宽为「明显的毛病」，所以城市、道路甚至菜单都能用这个词。

senses.title: A notorious person
senses.definition: a person whose name is widely known because of crimes or scandals
senses.definitionCN: 因罪行或丑闻而广为人知的人
senses.example: The notorious smuggler was finally caught at the border.
senses.exampleCN: 那个臭名昭著的走私犯终于在边境落网。
senses.why: The adjective attaches most naturally to the people whose names travel farthest, which is why it often sits before criminals and tyrants.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最自然地附着于名声传得最远的人身上，所以常放在罪犯与暴君之前。

senses.title: Places and products with a bad name
senses.titleCN: 名声不佳的地方与事物
senses.definition: describing a place, product, or brand that people associate with trouble or poor quality
senses.definitionCN: 形容人们与麻烦或低劣质量联系在一起的地方、产品或品牌
senses.example: The notorious shortcut through the marsh cost two drivers their cars.
senses.exampleCN: 那条穿过沼泽的臭名昭著的近路，让两位司机丢了车。
senses.why: A name spreads to whatever it touches, so roads, districts, and products inherit the bad fame of what happened there.
senses.whyCN: 名字会传到它所接触到的一切东西上，所以道路、街区与产品继承了在那里发生的事情的坏名声。

senses.title: Famous as a joke
senses.titleCN: 以玩笑般的坏名声而著名
senses.definition: humorously well known for an embarrassing or ridiculous trait
senses.definitionCN: 因令人尴尬或荒唐的特点而好笑地出名
senses.example: My notorious sense of direction once sent me into a broom closet.
senses.exampleCN: 我那出了名的糟糕方向感，有一次把我送进了扫帚间。
senses.why: Because the core is only public awareness, the word can be handed over to private jokes where nobody is really harmed.
senses.whyCN: 因为核心只是「万众皆知」，这个词也可以用在无人真正受害的私人玩笑里。

senses.title: Openly known, legal use
senses.definition: in legal writing, openly and generally known so that no evidence is needed
senses.definitionCN: 法律文本中，公开且普遍知晓，无须再提供证据
senses.example: The practice was notorious, so the court accepted it without testimony.
senses.exampleCN: 这一惯例众所周知，因此法院无须证词便予以采信。
senses.why: Law preserves the old neutral duty of notorius: what everyone openly knows proves itself.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了 notorius 古老的中立作用：人人都公开知道的事本身就足以证明自己。

senses.title: Stronger than infamous
senses.titleCN: 比 infamous 更侧重「人人都知」
senses.definition: expressing shock or disapproval at how widely a private shame has become public
senses.definitionCN: 表达对一桩私密丑事竟被广泛公开的震惊或不赞成
senses.example: It is notorious that the papers printed the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 众所周知，报纸把那封信印了出来。
senses.why: Where infamous lays on moral evil, notorious stresses the unbearable openness of the news.
senses.whyCN: infamous 侧重道德上的邪恶，而 notorious 强调消息被公开得令人难堪。

intro.en: Notorious comes from Latin notorius, well known, built on notus, known, and the -ous ending that English added for adjectives.

abstract.cn: 想象每根灯杆上都贴着悬赏告示，每张都是同一张脸。

abstract.en: Hear a name spoken in every cafe, always followed by a sigh.
abstract.cn: 想象每个咖啡馆里都有人提起同一个名字，后面总跟一声叹息。

abstract.en: Picture a queue of reporters outside one small house.
abstract.cn: 想象一排记者挤在一栋小房子门口。

examples.en: The bridge is notorious for collapsing in heavy rain.
examples.cn: 那座桥因大雨中坍塌而臭名昭著。

examples.en: A notorious gang once controlled the harbour.
examples.cn: 一个臭名昭著的黑帮曾控制着这座港口。

examples.en: She is notorious for arriving exactly on time.
examples.cn: 她以分秒不差地准时到达而出名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「no 托利亚死」——坏到没人愿意托付名字的人，自然臭名昭著；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 noscere（认识到）→ notus（已知的）→ notorius（广为人知的）→ 中世纪法语 notorieux → 英语 notorious，核心义从「人人皆知」转偏为「因坏事人人皆知」。

sensesIntro.en: Notorious starts from the neutral sense well known and modern English narrows it to bad fame, then lets it slide into qualities, people, places, and legal openness.
sensesIntro.cn: notorious 从中立的「广为人知」出发，现代英语把它收窄为「因坏事出名」，随后延伸到特点、人物、地方与法律上的公开性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face on a wanted poster that everyone recognises.
core.cn: 核心意象：人人都认得的那张通缉告示上的脸。

branches.en: Fame for something bad is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 因坏事出名是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Fame for a flaw loosens the badness into a mere fault.
branches.cn: 因某个毛病出名，把「坏」放宽为单纯的瑕疵。

branches.en: A notorious person is the most familiar use.
branches.cn: 臭名昭著的人是最常见的用法。

branches.en: Places and products, or private jokes, can wear the same label.
branches.cn: 地方与产品，乃至私人玩笑，都可以贴同一个标签。

branches.en: Legal openness and the comparison with infamous keep the neutral root visible.
branches.cn: 法律上的公开性与与 infamous 的对比，让中立的词根依然可见。

intro.en: Notorious is a Latin participle plus the adjective suffix -ous, with notorious, notoriety, and notoriously making up its family.
intro.cn: notorious 是拉丁语分词加上形容词词尾 -ous 构成，notorious、notoriety 与 notoriously 共同组成它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin notus means known, and the adjective notorius means well known.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 notus 意为已知的，形容词 notorius 意为广为人知的。

items.example: Noscere supplies the idea of knowing.
items.exampleCN: noscere 提供「知道」的概念。

items.example: Notus gives the stem not-.
items.exampleCN: notus 给出词干 not-。

items.example: Notorius is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: notorius 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous forms adjectives like notorius.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 notorius 这类形容词。

items.example: Notorious is the everyday adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: notorious 是词族最常用的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms notoriously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 notoriously。

items.example: Notoriously describes how widely something is known.
items.exampleCN: notoriously 描述某事被知晓的广泛程度。

items.meaningCN: 表示「……的状态或性质」的名词词尾
items.example: The noun suffix -ety helps build notoriety.
items.exampleCN: 名词词尾 -ety 帮助构成 notoriety。

items.example: Notoriety is the abstract noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: notoriety 是该词族的抽象名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态、性质的名词词尾（-ness）
items.example: The suffix -ness forms notoriousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 notoriousness。

definition_zh: 新手；初学者；修道院中的见习修士或修女
definition_en: a person new to a job, activity, or skill
core_image: 修道院门口的年轻人，穿着还没染色的素白长袍，第一次学着低头敲钟
scene: 修道院的台阶上，新来的人穿着还没染色的白袍，跟在老修士身后学敲钟。The novice rang the bell too slowly on his first morning in the monastery.
sceneCN: 这里 novice 是「见习修士」（第 4 个义项：进入修道院、尚未正式发愿的初修者）；句意：入修道院的那个早晨，见习修士敲钟敲得太慢了。

derivatives.zh: novice 加 -iate 构成的同源名词，义为「见习期；初修院」
novice 加 -hood 构成，义为「新手身份」，书面少见
novice 加 -like 构成的复合词，义为「像新手一样的」

senses.title: A beginner
senses.definition: someone who has just started to learn a job, sport, or skill
senses.definitionCN: 刚开始学习某一工作、运动或技能的人
senses.example: As a novice, she spent more time watching than playing.
senses.exampleCN: 作为新手，她看的时间比打的时间还长。
senses.why: The Latin source novicius means newly arrived, so the first and plainest sense is simply someone who has only just come in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 novicius 意为「新来的」，所以最直接、最本来的义项就是刚刚加入的人。

senses.title: Amateur, not yet a master
senses.titleCN: 非专业者；未出师的学手
senses.definition: a person who does an activity for enjoyment, not as a trained professional
senses.definitionCN: 以兴趣爱好而非受过训练的专业身份从事某项活动的人
senses.example: The workshop welcomes novices as well as experts.
senses.exampleCN: 这个工作坊既欢迎专家，也欢迎非专业者。
senses.why: If the word only marks where you stand on a ladder of skill, everyone below the master counts, including the happy amateur.
senses.whyCN: 如果这个词只标示你在技能阶梯上的位置，那么大师以下的人都算，包括乐在其中的业余者。

senses.title: An inexperienced user
senses.definition: someone unfamiliar with a tool, place, or system and likely to misuse it
senses.definitionCN: 对某一工具、场所或系统不熟悉、容易误用的人
senses.example: A novice can easily delete the whole folder by mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 不熟练的使用者很容易误删整个文件夹。
senses.why: Every skill begins with novelty, so the newcomer to a machine is a novice in exactly the sense the word began with.
senses.whyCN: 每种技能都从新鲜开始，所以初来接触机器的人，正是这个词最初那种意义上的新手。

senses.title: A trainee in a monastery
senses.definition: a person preparing to join a religious order before taking final vows
senses.definitionCN: 准备加入修会、尚未正式发愿的人
senses.example: The novice washed the dishes before the evening prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 见习修士在晚祷前洗了碗碟。
senses.why: The oldest English use is this religious one: a newcomer inside a community, under training, not yet a full member.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最古老的用法：社区里的新来者，正在受训，还不是正式成员。

senses.title: A new participant in a programme
senses.definition: a new member of an organisation or event who is still learning its rules
senses.definitionCN: 刚加入某个组织或活动、还在学习其规则的新成员
senses.example: The festival has a special track for novices.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆为初入者专门设置了一条路线。
senses.why: Once the word means any newcomer, clubs, races, and fairs all need a word for the person on the first step.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词泛指任何新来者，俱乐部、比赛和集会都需要一个词来指处于第一步的人。

senses.title: An easy first stage
senses.definition: the simple introductory stage of a course or task rather than the person in it
senses.definitionCN: 课程或任务中简单的入门阶段，而非处在其中的人
senses.example: The book stays at novice level for the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书前半部分一直停留在入门水平。
senses.why: People use the person noun as a label for the level, because the stage is defined by the kind of person who belongs to it.
senses.whyCN: 人们用指人的名词来标示水平，因为这个阶段正是由属于它的人来定义的。

senses.title: Someone new and untested
senses.definition: a newcomer in a group who has not yet proved himself or herself
senses.definitionCN: 群体中尚未证明自己的新成员
senses.example: The team captain is still a novice in international matches.
senses.exampleCN: 这位队长在国际赛场上仍是新人。
senses.why: Novelty also carries a hint of doubt, so the word can point at character, not just at skill.
senses.whyCN: 「新」还带着一丝怀疑，所以这个词不仅指技能，也可以指向品格与经历。

intro.en: Novice comes from Latin novicius, newly arrived, built on novus, new, through Old French novice.
intro.cn: novice 来自拉丁语 novicius（新来的），由 novus（新的）构成，经古法语 novice 进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root newo- gives the idea of something new; the form is a reconstruction, not a written word.
items.cn: 重构词根 newo- 表示「新的」；该形式是重构结果，并非有文献记载的词。

items.en: The Latin adjective novus means new and gives the whole family of English new words.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 novus 意为「新的」，为英语的「新」类词汇提供基础。

items.en: Novicius means newly come or newly arrived, used of slaves and newcomers.
items.cn: novicius 意为「新来的、新到任的」，既用于奴隶，也用于新来的人。

items.en: Old French novice names a beginner, especially in a religious house.
items.cn: 古法语 novice 指初学者，尤指修道院里的新入者。

items.en: The word enters English first for the trainee in a monastery.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语时，首先指修道院中的见习者。

items.en: The meaning widens to any beginner in any skill.
items.cn: 含义扩大为任何领域的初学者。

note.en: Novice is the noun of being new, close to the Latin nov- family and to the ordinary beginner words.
note.cn: novice 是表示「新」的名词，与拉丁语 nov- 词族以及普通的「初学者」词相邻。

entries.definition: new and unusual; the same Latin novus lies behind it
entries.definitionCN: 新奇的；同源于拉丁语 novus

entries.definition: the period of being a novice in a religious order
entries.definitionCN: 见习期；初修院

entries.definition: attention or a written warning; the spelling looks close but the history is different
entries.definitionCN: 注意；通知；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: someone who is just starting to learn
entries.definitionCN: 初学者；新手

entries.definition: a learner bound to a skilled master to learn a trade
entries.definitionCN: 学徒（跟随师傅学手艺）

entries.definition: a person with deep knowledge or skill
entries.definitionCN: 专家；行家

normalIntro.en: Novice is the newest person in the room, still learning where to stand.
normalIntro.cn: novice 是房间里最新来的那个人，还在学该站在哪里。

normal.en: The Latin novus, new, sits inside novice and also gives novel and novelty.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 novus（新的）藏在 novice 里，也构成 novel 与 novelty。

normal.en: Complete novice is the usual phrase for someone who knows nothing yet.
normal.cn: complete novice 是表示「完全的新手」的常用说法。

normal.en: A novice at something stresses the field, while a novice in something stresses the role or group.
normal.cn: a novice at 某个技能突出领域，a novice in 某处或某组织突出身份与群体。

normal.en: The religious trainee sense is the oldest English use and still lives in novitiate.
normal.cn: 修道院见习者的含义是英语中最早的用法，至今仍保留在 novitiate 一词里。

normal.en: Compare beginner: beginner is plainer and friendlier, novice is more formal and slightly technical.
normal.cn: 对比 beginner：beginner 更朴素亲切，novice 更正式、也稍带技术性。

abstract.en: Picture a white robe walking behind a grey one along a cloister.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊里一件白袍跟在一件灰袍后面走。

abstract.en: See a first day at a new desk, with every drawer still empty.
abstract.cn: 想象新工位的第一天，每个抽屉都还空着。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand hovering over a keyboard, unsure which key is safe.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手悬在键盘上方，不知道哪个键按了才安全。

examples.en: Even a novice can follow this recipe.
examples.cn: 连新手都能照着这个食谱做出来。

examples.en: The course is designed for complete novices.
examples.cn: 这门课程是为完全的新手设计的。

examples.en: The old abbot trained many novices in the same hall.
examples.cn: 老院长在同一间厅堂里带过多名见习修士。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「no 味似」——第一次上场「没味似」，什么都还没上手，就是新手；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 重构词根 newo-（新的）→ 拉丁语 novus（新的）→ novicius（新来的）→ 古法语 novice → 中古英语 novice（修道院见习者）→ 现代英语泛指新手。

sensesIntro.en: Novice begins with the newly arrived person, widens to any beginner or amateur, and then stretches to the level that belongs to such people.
sensesIntro.cn: novice 从「新来的人」出发，扩大到任何初学者或业余者，再延伸到属于这类人的水平阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newcomer in a plain white robe, still learning the routine.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿着素白长袍的新来者，还在学习日常流程。

branches.en: A plain beginner is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 普通的初学者是日常义项。

branches.en: The amateur is defined by standing below the master.
branches.cn: 非专业者是由处在师者之下这一定位来界定的。

branches.en: The inexperienced user carries the risk of misuse.
branches.cn: 不熟练的使用者带有误用的风险。

branches.en: Religious trainees and new participants are the oldest and earliest forms of the word.
branches.cn: 宗教见习者与新参加者是这个词最古老的形态。

branches.en: A level and an untested newcomer both grow out of the basic image.
branches.cn: 一个水平阶段与一个未经考验的新人，都从基本意象长出来。

intro.en: Novice is a member of the Latin nov- family of newness, alongside novel, novelty, and novitiate.
intro.cn: novice 属于拉丁语 nov-（新）词族，与 novel、novelty、novitiate 并列。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus means new, and novicius means newly arrived.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus 意为新的，novicius 意为新来的。

items.example: Novus gives the nov- stem to English.
items.exampleCN: novus 为英语提供 nov- 词干。

items.example: Novicius is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: novicius 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.example: Novice is the everyday noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: novice 是词族最常用的名词。

items.example: Novel repeats the idea of newness.
items.exampleCN: novel 重复了「新」这一概念。

items.example: Novelty names the state of being new.
items.exampleCN: novelty 表示「新」的状态。

items.meaning: the period of a religious novice
items.example: Novitiate names the period of a novice.
items.exampleCN: novitiate 指见习者的见习期。

items.example: Renovate renews an old building.
items.exampleCN: renovate 使旧建筑焕然一新。

items.example: Innovation carries the same new root.
items.exampleCN: innovation 同样带着「新」的词根。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms renovate and innovate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 renovate 和 innovate。

items.meaningCN: 表示人或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The Old French ending -ice forms novice.
items.exampleCN: 古法语词尾 -ice 构成 novice。

definition_zh: 有害的；有毒的；令人厌恶的；败坏道德的；伤害健康的
definition_en: harmful or poisonous, especially to health, and by extension deeply unpleasant or morally damaging
core_image: 密室里一缕灰黄气体从裂缝飘出，碰到它的植物叶尖先发黑
scene: 实验室通风不好，墙角冒出呛人的烟，学生们捂着口鼻往外走。The noxious fumes spread through the basement faster than anyone could open a window.
sceneCN: 这里 noxious 是「有毒的、有害的」（第 1 个义项：气体或物质对身体有害）；句意：有害的浓烟扩散得很快，快到没人来得及打开窗户。

pos.zh: 形容词：有害的；有毒的；令人厌恶的；败坏道德的

derivatives.zh: 由 noxious 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「有害性；毒性」
由拉丁语前缀 ob-（朝向、暴露于）加同一词根构成，原义「暴露于伤害的、该受罚的」，现代义为「讨人厌的；可憎的」
由否定前缀 in- 加 nocuous（有害的）构成，义为「无害的；无恶意的」，是 noxious 的反义同根词
与 noxious 同出拉丁语 nocere，义为「有害的；有毒的」，是较古旧、较罕见的同义词

senses.title: Poisonous to the body
senses.definition: containing a substance that harms or poisons people, animals, or plants when taken in
senses.definitionCN: 含有毒害作用的物质，吸入或摄入后会伤害人、动物或植物
senses.example: The noxious fumes from the burning plastic drove the workers out of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 塑料燃烧产生的有毒浓烟把工人逼出了厂房。
senses.why: Latin noxa is harm and nocere is to hurt, so the adjective names whatever hurts the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 noxa 是「伤害」，nocere 是「造成伤害」，所以这个形容词命名的是会伤身的东西。

senses.title: Harmful in a general way
senses.titleCN: 有害的；对新事物不利的
senses.definition: damaging to health, growth, or a system, without any idea of actual poison
senses.definitionCN: 对健康、生长或某个体系造成损害，但不一定真的有毒性
senses.example: Some farmers treat the weed as noxious and pull it out before it seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 有些农民把这种杂草视为有害之物，在它结籽前就拔掉。
senses.why: Because harm can be slow and indirect, the word also covers things that damage growth or order rather than poison.
senses.whyCN: 因为伤害可以是缓慢、间接的，这个词也覆盖损害生长或秩序、而非毒死人的事物。

senses.title: Revolting to the senses
senses.definition: so unpleasant to smell or look at that a person turns away from it
senses.definitionCN: 气味或外观极其难闻难看，让人本能地躲开
senses.example: A noxious smell rose from the drain beside the fish market.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼市旁的排水沟里冒出一股恶臭。
senses.why: The nose reports harm before a doctor does, so a smell that hurts is easily called noxious.
senses.whyCN: 鼻子比医生更早报告伤害，所以刺鼻伤人的气味很容易被叫作 noxious。

senses.title: Moral poison
senses.definition: corrupting in effect, especially ideas or influences that damage a healthy mind or society
senses.definitionCN: 在效果上起腐蚀作用，尤指损害健全心智或社会的观念与影响
senses.example: The essay warned against the noxious influence of media money on honest reporting.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章警告媒体金钱对诚实报道的有害影响。
senses.why: If gas can poison a room, an idea can poison a mind, and the same adjective is reused for moral harm.
senses.whyCN: 毒气能毒化一间屋子，观念就能毒化一颗头脑，同一个形容词便被挪用到道德伤害上。

senses.title: Legally obnoxious, a lost older sense
senses.titleCN: 违法的；应受惩处的（旧义）
senses.definition: in older legal English, liable to punishment or contrary to law, a sense now taken over by obnoxious
senses.definitionCN: 在早期法律英语中指「应受惩处的；违反法律的」，这一义项后来被 obnoxious 承接
senses.example: The old statute calls such a trade noxious and punishable.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧法规把这种买卖定为违法并应予惩罚。
senses.why: Latin noxius also meant guilty or liable, and that legal strand later split off into obnoxious.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 noxius 也有「有罪的、该担责的」之意，这条法律支脉后来分裂出去，成为 obnoxious。

intro.en: Noxious is a Latin adjective for anything that hurts, built on the same stem that gives innocent and obnoxious.
intro.cn: noxious 是拉丁语中表示「会造成伤害」的形容词，与 innocent、obnoxious 共用同一词干。

items.en: Noxa means harm or injury, and noxius means harmful or guilty.
items.cn: 拉丁语 noxa 意为「伤害、损害」，noxius 意为「有害的」，同时带有「有罪的」意味。

items.en: The verb nocere, to hurt, is the engine of the family and also lies inside innocent.
items.cn: 动词 nocere（伤害）是整个词族的发动机，也藏在 innocent（无害的）里面。

items.en: Roman legal writers used noxius for acts and things that deserved punishment.
items.cn: 罗马法学作者用 noxius 指应当受罚的行为与物件。

items.en: English takes noxious from Latin in the sixteenth century, first for poisons and diseased air.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁语引入 noxious，最初用于毒物与致病的空气。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense, adds the moral one, and splits the legal sense off into obnoxious.
items.cn: 现代英语保留物质义，添上道德义，并把法律义分支拱手让给 obnoxious。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on Latin nocere; the near-meaning group gathers words for poison, harm, and disgust.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语 nocere 构成的词；近义组收表示有毒、有害与厌恶的词。

entries.definition: harmless and unlikely to offend anyone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无害的、不冒犯人的」；由 in- 加 nocuous 构成，与 noxious 同根而义相反。

entries.definition: very unpleasant or offensive in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「讨人厌的、可憎的」；与 noxious 同出 nocere，加了前缀 ob-，语义偏向「令人反感」。

entries.definition: harmful or noxious, the older and rarer partner of the modern word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有害的、有毒的」；是 noxious 更古老、更罕见的同源词。

entries.definition: the quality of being harmful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有害性、毒性」；由 noxious 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: poisonous, coming from Greek for a bow and arrow poison.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有毒的」；词源是希腊语中涂在箭上的毒，现代多用于化学与医学语境。

entries.definition: containing poison, the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有毒的」；是最日常、最直白的说法。

entries.definition: causing damage of any kind, without suggesting poison.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有害的」；泛指造成任何损害，不暗示毒性，语气比 noxious 轻。

entries.definition: dirty and revolting to the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「污浊的、难闻恶心的」；对应 noxious 的感官义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow Latin noxa, the nocere family, and the collocations English fixed around the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依据拉丁语 noxa、nocere 词族，以及英语固定下来的搭配。

normal.en: Noxa is harm, so noxious is harm turned into an adjective.
normal.cn: noxa 是伤害，所以 noxious 就是把伤害做成形容词。

normal.en: Innocent shares the same stem: in- plus nocere means not hurting.
normal.cn: innocent 藏着同一词干：in- 加 nocere，就是「不伤害」。

normal.en: Obnoxious adds ob- to the same root and moves the harm into bad manners.
normal.cn: obnoxious 在同一词根上加 ob-，把伤害挪到了讨厌的举止上。

normal.en: Noxious fumes is the phrase most examiners expect to see.
normal.cn: noxious fumes 是考试中最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Toxic is the laboratory word, noxious leans toward air, smoke, and weeds.
normal.cn: toxic 更偏实验室语境，noxious 更偏空气、烟和杂草。

abstract.en: Picture a grey-yellow gas creeping out of a crack and blackening the tips of nearby leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一缕灰黄气体从裂缝里爬出，把附近叶子的尖端染黑。

abstract.en: Picture a weed field that the law marks with a red sign as noxious.
abstract.cn: 想象一片被法律用红色标牌标记为有害的杂草丛。

abstract.en: Picture a boy holding his nose and running past an open drain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男孩捏着鼻子跑过敞开的排水沟。

examples.en: The plant was fined for releasing noxious gases into the river valley.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因向河谷排放有毒气体而被罚款。

examples.en: Officials listed the plant as a noxious weed in every southern state.
examples.cn: 官员们把这种植物列为南方各州的害草。

examples.en: The noxious smell of the chemical store made the children sick.
examples.cn: 化学品仓库的恶臭让孩子们感到不适。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nox」近似「脑壳」——闻到毒气，脑壳先疼；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 noxa（伤害）+ -ius（形容词后缀）→ noxius（有害的；有罪的）→ 英语 noxious。同族有 nocere（伤害）、innocent 与 obnoxious，核心义是「会造成伤害」。

sensesIntro.en: One adjective grows outward from harm: poison in the body, general damage, a smell that drives people off, and finally poison in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个形容词从「伤害」向外生长：进身的毒、泛指的损害、让人躲开的气味，最后是毒害心灵的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey-yellow gas slipping out of a crack and turning the leaf tips black.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰黄气体从裂缝飘出，把叶尖染黑。

branches.en: THE BODY: poison that harms the lungs is the first sense.
branches.cn: 身体线：伤害肺部的毒是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: slow damage to crops, order, or growth without any poison.
branches.cn: 体系线：对作物、秩序或生长的慢性损害，未必有毒。

branches.en: THE SENSES: a smell that hurts is reported as noxious.
branches.cn: 感官线：刺鼻伤人的气味直接被称为 noxious。

branches.en: THE MIND: ideas and influences borrow the poison image.
branches.cn: 心智线：观念与影响借用了「毒」的意象。

branches.en: THE LAW: the old sense of liable to punishment survives in obnoxious.
branches.cn: 法律线：旧的「应受惩处」义在 obnoxious 中延续。

intro.en: Noxious is a Latin adjective with three English suffixes and a rich family around the verb nocere.
intro.cn: noxious 是拉丁语形容词，英语里有三个常见后缀，围绕动词 nocere 还有一整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin noxa, noxius, and nocere are all recorded; innocuous and innocent share the same negated stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 noxa、noxius、nocere 均有记录；innocuous 与 innocent 共享同一否定词干。

items.example: Noxa is the harm that the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: noxa 是这个形容词所描述的伤害。

items.example: Noxius is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: noxius 就是英语词号的直接祖先。

items.example: Nocere is the engine of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: nocere 是整个词族的发动机。

items.meaning: full of, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix -ous forms noxious from noxa.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 由 noxa 构成 noxious。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms noxiousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 noxiousness。

items.example: The prefix in- makes innocuous from nocuous.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 nocuous 变成 innocuous。

items.example: The prefix ob- builds obnoxious, a word for offensive conduct.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ob- 构成 obnoxious，指令人反感的举止。

items.example: The suffix -ive builds nocive, a rare synonym.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成罕见的同义词 nocive。

items.example: Noxiousness names the harm in the abstract.
items.exampleCN: noxiousness 抽象地命名有害的性质。

definition_zh: 金块；小块东西；有价值的信息；要点；鸡块
definition_en: a small lump of a precious metal or other solid, and by extension a small but valuable piece of information, food, or wisdom
core_image: 溪水退去，泥砂之间露出一块沾满沙子的金黄色疙瘩
scene: 淘金者蹲在小溪边，把筛子里的砂石倒进盆里，水一冲，几粒沙金底下压着一块沉甸甸的硬物。A nugget the size of his thumb flashed up from the pan and every man on the bank stopped digging.
sceneCN: 这里 nugget 是「金块」（第 1 个义项：淘洗出来的一小块天然金属）；句意为：一块拇指大的金块从淘金盆里闪出来，岸上所有掘金者手上的活都停了。

pos.zh: 名词：金块；小块；有价值的信息；要点；鸡块

collocations.zh: 一块金子；一块天然金块

derivatives.zh: 由 nugget 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，口语中义为「像小金块似的；块状的」，多用于矿工行话与澳大利亚口语
gold 加 nugget 构成的复合名词，义为「天然金块」，是最常用的固定说法

senses.title: A natural lump of precious metal
senses.definition: a rough lump of gold or another precious metal found in the earth rather than shaped by a smith
senses.definitionCN: 从地里挖出来、未经工匠打制的一块原生金属，多为金子
senses.example: A prospector found a nugget of gold in the creek bed.
senses.exampleCN: 一名淘金者在小溪河床里找到一块金块。
senses.why: The word seems to grow out of dialect nug, a lump, and the gold fields of the nineteenth century fixed it to metal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词大概由方言词 nug（疙瘩、块）派生而来，十九世纪的金矿热把它牢牢固定在金属上。

senses.title: Any small solid lump
senses.definition: a small compact lump of some solid substance, such as coal, ore, or sugar
senses.definitionCN: 某种固体的一小块、一小团，如煤块、矿石或糖块
senses.example: The fire was fed with a few nuggets of coal.
senses.exampleCN: 炉火靠几块煤疙瘩维持着。
senses.why: Once the word meant lump, it could be moved from gold to coal, ore, and any shaped solid.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「块状物」成了词义，就可以从金子挪到煤、矿石以及任何成块的固体上。

senses.title: A valuable piece of information
senses.definition: a small unit of useful information, insight, or advice that is worth keeping out of a much larger amount
senses.definitionCN: 从大量材料里挑出的一小条有用信息、洞见或建议，值得留存
senses.example: Every chapter offers a few nuggets of practical advice on saving money.
senses.exampleCN: 每一章都会给出几条关于省钱的实用建议。
senses.why: Gold is rare and valuable, so a precious fact hidden in a long report is pictured as a lump of gold in the dirt.
senses.whyCN: 金子稀有而贵重，所以长报告里藏着的宝贵事实，就被想象成泥土中的金块。

senses.title: The small but tasty part of a dish
senses.definition: a small cooked piece of food, especially of breaded chicken, sold and eaten on its own
senses.definitionCN: 一小块烹制好的食物，尤指裹面包屑的鸡肉块，可单卖单吃
senses.example: The children shared a plate of fried chicken nuggets.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们分了一盘炸鸡块。
senses.why: Food is cut into nuggets so each piece is a solid lump, and the fast-food trade made the small sense famous.
senses.whyCN: 食物被切成 nugget，就是让每一块都是实心的疙瘩，快餐业让这个小块义沿用开来。

senses.title: A short item in a digest
senses.titleCN: 短小精悍的片段；摘要条目
senses.definition: a short, tightly written section or item, such as one paragraph of a digest or one point in a list
senses.definitionCN: 短小紧凑的一段或一条，如文摘中的一段、清单中的一条
senses.example: The newsletter rounds up the week in six nuggets of news.
senses.exampleCN: 这份简报用六条短新闻总结了一周。
senses.why: Because a nugget is small and self-contained, editors use the word for a dense readable block of text.
senses.whyCN: 因为 nugget 小而成块，编辑就用它来称一段密集、可独立阅读的文字。

intro.en: Nugget is a native English word of uncertain origin, probably from a dialect noun for a lump, and it was the gold rushes that made it famous.
intro.cn: nugget 是本土英语词，来源不确定，一般认为来自表示「疙瘩、块」的方言名词，是淘金热让它为人熟知。

items.en: A dialect noun nug and an adjective nuggy, both meaning a lump or a stubby thing, are recorded in English dialects.
items.cn: 英语方言中记录了名词 nug 与形容词 nuggy，都表示「疙瘩、粗短的东西」。

items.en: Nugget appears in the early nineteenth century in the sense of a lump, especially of metal, and the origin of the form remains uncertain.
items.cn: nugget 在十九世纪初以「疙瘩、块」之义出现，尤指金属块；这个词形的具体来源至今存疑。

items.en: The California and Australian gold rushes spread the word for a lump of gold around the world.
items.cn: 加利福尼亚与澳大利亚的淘金热把这个指金块的词传遍世界。

items.en: The figurative use for a valuable piece of information is recorded in the later nineteenth century.
items.cn: 指「有价值的信息」的比喻用法在十九世纪后期已有记录。

items.en: Modern English uses nugget for wisdom, news items, and fast-food chicken pieces.
items.cn: 现代英语用 nugget 指箴言、新闻短条与快餐鸡块。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with a similar shape or build; the near-meaning group gathers words for lumps, ore, and small precious bits.
note.cn: 形近组收外形或构词相近的词；近义组收表示块状物、矿石与微小珍贵之物的词。

entries.definition: pushed lightly with the elbow to draw attention.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 nudge 的过去式，义为「用肘轻推」；只是拼写相近，词源完全不同。

entries.definition: lumpy or gold-bearing in miners speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「块状的、含金块的」；由 nugget 加 -y 构成，多见于矿工行话。

entries.definition: a small clever tool or device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小装置、小玩意」；与 nugget 尾音相近，只是发音相像，词源无关。

entries.definition: a solid piece of something with no regular shape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「块、疙瘩」；是最通用的说法，没有 nugget 的珍贵色彩。

entries.definition: a thick piece cut or broken off something larger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大块、厚块」；强调从大块上切下或掰下的粗块。

entries.definition: a bar of metal cast into a standard shape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「铸锭」；指熔铸成标准形状的金属条，与天然金块正好相反。

entries.definition: a small smooth rounded stone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鹅卵石」；指被水磨圆的小石子，形状规则而圆滑。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the dialect lump behind the word, the gold rush it came from, and its figurative life today.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依据词后的方言词「块」、它来自的淘金热，以及它今天的比喻用法。

normal.en: Nug is an old dialect word for a lump, so a nugget is a small lump.
normal.cn: nug 是古方言里「疙瘩、块」的说法，所以 nugget 就是一小块。

normal.en: The gold rush gave us nuggets of gold, and the phrase stuck.
normal.cn: 淘金热带来了 nuggets of gold 这一说法，并固定下来。

normal.en: A newspaper nugget is a short packed paragraph, like a lump of facts.
normal.cn: 报纸上的 nugget 是一段短而密实的文字，像一块压缩的事实。

normal.en: Compare ingot: an ingot is poured into shape, a nugget is found as it is.
normal.cn: 对比 ingot：铸锭是浇铸成形的，金块是天然长成的。

normal.en: Chicken nuggets are simply lumps of breaded chicken.
normal.cn: chicken nuggets 不过是裹了面包屑的鸡肉疙瘩。

abstract.en: Picture muddy water draining away and leaving a dull yellow lump in the pan.
abstract.cn: 想象浑水退去，淘金盆底留下一块暗黄的疙瘩。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of coal sitting among a heap of dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆粉尘里坐着一块煤。

abstract.en: Picture a long dull report with one shining sentence underlined in red.
abstract.cn: 想象一份又长又闷的报告，其中一句被红色下划线标得发亮。

examples.en: The museum displays the largest gold nugget ever found in the region.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出了本地区发现过的最大一块金块。

examples.en: Her talk was full of nuggets of advice for first-time parents.
examples.cn: 她的讲座里满是对新手父母的宝贵建议。

examples.en: He ordered chicken nuggets and a small drink.
examples.cn: 他点了一份鸡块和一杯小杯饮料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拿个它」——捡到一块金子，赶紧「拿个它」走；这只是读音联想，不是词源。

root: 一般认为来自英语方言名词 nug（疙瘩、块）与形容词 nuggy（粗短的），加指小词尾 -et 成为 nugget；词形来源不确定，十九世纪因加州与澳洲淘金热而通行。

sensesIntro.en: From one idea of a small solid lump, the word travels to gold, to coal, to precious information, to food, and to short news items.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个「小块实体」的概念出发，这个词走到金子、煤炭、宝贵信息、食物，再到短小新闻条。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a muddy handful with one solid yellow lump glinting at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把泥沙里，一块实心金黄色疙瘩在盆底反光。

branches.en: THE ORE: a natural lump of gold is where the word starts.
branches.cn: 矿石线：天然金块是这个词的起点。

branches.en: THE LUMP: coal, ore, and sugar inherit the plain sense of a solid piece.
branches.cn: 块状线：煤、矿石与糖继承了「实心一块」的朴素义。

branches.en: THE MIND: the rarest and most valuable facts become mental gold.
branches.cn: 心智线：最稀有、最宝贵的事实变成脑中的金子。

branches.en: THE PLATE: fast food cuts a dish into small lumps.
branches.cn: 餐盘线：快餐把菜肴切成一块块。

branches.en: THE PAGE: editors borrow the small self-contained lump for short items.
branches.cn: 版面线：编辑借用「自成一体的小块」来称呼短条目。

intro.en: Nugget is a native dialect formation, so the English suffixes and compounds around it matter more than Latin ones.
intro.cn: nugget 是本土方言构词，所以围绕它的英语后缀与复合词比拉丁成分更重要。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is recorded for this word, and the affix -et is a French diminutive that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可考的拉丁语祖先，后缀 -et 是英语从法语借来的指小词尾。

items.example: Nug is the dialect lump behind the word.
items.exampleCN: nug 是这个词背后的方言词「块」。

items.example: The adjective nuggy describes a stubby, lumpy thing.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 nuggy 描述粗短、成块的东西。

items.example: The suffix -et marks something small, as in nugget.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -et 标记「小」，nugget 正是如此。

items.example: Gold plus nugget makes the fixed phrase gold nugget.
items.exampleCN: gold 加 nugget 构成固定说法 gold nugget。

items.example: The suffix -y forms nuggety.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 nuggety。

items.example: The plural suffix forms nuggets.
items.exampleCN: 复数后缀构成 nuggets。

items.example: Chicken plus nugget gives the fast-food compound.
items.exampleCN: chicken 加 nugget 构成快餐复合词。

items.meaning: a person who prepares writing for publication
items.example: Editors call a short packed item a nugget.
items.exampleCN: 编辑把短小密集的条目称作 nugget。

items.example: Nuggety is a miners word for ore full of lumps.
items.exampleCN: nuggety 是矿工形容满是金块的矿石的用词。

definition_zh: 零；无效的；无法律效力的；无意义的；空值；无的
definition_en: having no legal force, or having no value, number, or meaning; in computing, a special empty value that is not zero
core_image: 一张盖了钢印的契约被法官用红笔划掉，纸上一片空白
scene: 法官看完合同，发现签字的人当时已经成年，却精神失常，法律上并不具备缔约能力。The judge ruled the contract null, and the estate was divided as if it had never been signed.
sceneCN: 这里 null 是「无效的、无法律效力的」（第 1 个义项：法律上不成立、不被承认）；句意：法官裁定合同无效，遗产的分法就好像它从未被签署过一样。

pos.zh: 形容词：零的；无效的；无法律效力的；无意义的

collocations.zh: 零结果；未发现显著差异的结果

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语词根 null- 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「无效；无效状态」
由词根 null- 加动词后缀 -ify 构成，义为「使在法律上失效；废止」
由 nullify 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「废止；无效宣告」
由拉丁语 ad- 加 nullus 构成，经古法语进入英语，义为「废除；取消」（婚姻、判决等）

senses.title: Having no legal force
senses.definition: no longer binding in law, as if the document or act had never existed
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上不再有约束力，就好像文书或行为从来没有存在过
senses.example: The judge declared the contract null and void.
senses.exampleCN: 法官宣布这份合同无效。
senses.why: Latin nullus means not any or none, so something null is nothing in the eyes of the law.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nullus 意为「一个也没有」，所以在法律眼里，null 的东西就等于不存在。

senses.title: Of no value or no force
senses.definition: worthless or cancelled out completely, used of votes, effort, or rights
senses.definitionCN: 没有价值或完全被抵消，用于选票、努力或权利
senses.example: Without a quorum the vote becomes null.
senses.exampleCN: 没有法定人数，这次投票就作废。
senses.why: If the result is nothing, the thing that produced it counts for nothing too.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果是一片空白，产生结果的东西也就算不上什么。

senses.title: Zero in mathematics
senses.definition: equal to zero, used in technical contexts such as the null vector or the null set
senses.definitionCN: 等于零，用于空向量、空集等技术语境
senses.example: The field is zero everywhere, a null vector.
senses.exampleCN: 这个场处处为零，是一个零向量。
senses.why: Latin nullus meant none, and in mathematics none became the number zero.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nullus 意为「一个都没有」，在数学里「没有」就变成了数字零。

senses.title: Not significant in statistics
senses.definition: in statistics, showing no difference from what chance would produce, as in a null result or the null hypothesis
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中没有显示出与随机波动不同的差异，如零结果与零假设
senses.example: The trial produced a null result, so the drug was not approved.
senses.exampleCN: 试验得到了零结果，因此这种药未获批准。
senses.why: A hypothesis of nothing, stating that no effect exists, is named with the word for none.
senses.whyCN: 一种声称「不存在效应」的假设，就用表示「无」的词来命名。

senses.title: An empty computer value
senses.definition: in computing, a special value that means no value has been set, different from the number zero
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中表示「尚未赋值」的特殊值，与数字零并不相同
senses.example: The program crashed because a key was set to null.
senses.exampleCN: 程序崩溃了，因为有一个键被设成了空值。
senses.why: A field that holds nothing is the modern digital version of nullus, none of any kind.
senses.whyCN: 一个什么都不装的字段，就是 nullus「什么都没有」的现代数字版。

senses.title: In the fixed phrase null and void
senses.definition: in the legal doublet null and void, where the Latin word stands beside a French word that means the same
senses.definitionCN: 用于法律双式短语 null and void：拉丁词与法语同义词并排，同指「无效」
senses.example: Any clause added after signing is null and void.
senses.exampleCN: 签署后添加的任何条款都无效。
senses.why: English law liked pairs of near-synonyms from Latin and French, and this pair survived as a formula.
senses.whyCN: 英国法律喜欢把拉丁语与法语近义词并排，这一对作为程式化套语留了下来。

intro.en: Null is a legal Latin adjective for zero, and it survives mainly in law, mathematics, and computing.
intro.cn: null 是拉丁语法律用语中表示「零」的形容词，主要活在法律、数学与计算机领域。

items.en: Latin nullus, meaning not any or none, is formed from ne plus ullus, not any.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nullus 意为「一个也没有」，由否定词 ne 加 ullus（任何一个）构成。

items.en: In classical Latin the two parts fused into one negative pronoun that behaves like no one.
items.cn: 在古典拉丁语中，这两部分融合成一个充当否定代词的词，用法类似「没有人」。

items.en: Legal Latin used nullus for documents and acts that had no force, and that usage entered English.
items.cn: 中世纪法律拉丁语用 nullus 指没有效力的文书与行为，这一用法进入英语。

items.en: English takes null through legal writing, and the phrase null and void appears in the record.
items.cn: 英语通过法律文书引入 null，短语 null and void 见诸文字记载。

items.en: Modern English adds mathematics, statistics, and the computing sense of a value that is not zero.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了数学、统计学的用法，以及计算机中「不等于零的空值」义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin null- stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for empty, void, and nothing.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语 null- 词干构成的词；近义组收表示「空、无、作废」的词。

entries.definition: to make something legally void or ineffective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使在法律上失效、废止」；由同一词根加动词后缀 -ify 构成。

entries.definition: the state of being legally void.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无效、无效状态」；由同一词根加 -ity 构成，是法律用语。

entries.definition: to cancel a marriage or a ruling completely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废除、取消」（婚姻或裁决）；由拉丁语 ad- 加 nullus 构成，与 null 同源。

entries.definition: the act of making something void, as of a law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废止、宣告无效」；由 nullify 加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: not valid and having no legal effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无效的」；来自古法语，与 null 组成法律套语 null and void。

entries.definition: not legally or officially acceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无效的、不能接受的」；多指证件、票据或论据不被承认。

entries.definition: nothing, or zero, in accounts and in sport.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无、零」；常用在账目、比赛比分里。

entries.definition: the number 0, from an Arabic root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「零」；是普通的数字说法，没有 null 的「无效」含义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow Latin nullus, the legal doublet, and the technical senses that keep the word alive.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依据拉丁语 nullus、法律双式短语，以及让这个词继续存活的技术含义。

normal.en: Nullus is ne plus ullus: not any, so null means none of anything.
normal.cn: nullus 是 ne 加 ullus：不是任何一个，所以 null 就是「什么也没有」。

normal.en: Null and void pairs a Latin word with a French word for the same idea.
normal.cn: null and void 把拉丁词与法语同义词并排成对。

normal.en: Nullify and nullity both keep the null- stem and stay in legal and formal use.
normal.cn: nullify 与 nullity 都保留 null- 词干，用于法律与正式场合。

normal.en: A null result in science means no effect was found, not that the test failed.
normal.cn: 科学中的 null result 指没找到效应，而不是实验失败。

normal.en: In computing null is empty, while zero is a number that exists.
normal.cn: 计算机里 null 是什么都没有，零却是一个确实存在的数。

abstract.en: Picture a stamped contract crossed out in red until the page is blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一份盖章的合同被红笔划掉，直到整页空白。

abstract.en: Picture an empty box on a form where a signature should be.
abstract.cn: 想象表格上该签名的地方留着一个空框。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard showing nothing at all, not even a zero.
abstract.cn: 想象记分牌上连零都没有，只有一片空白。

examples.en: The agreement was declared null because the buyer was under age.
examples.cn: 由于买方未成年，这份协议被宣告无效。

examples.en: The study found a null result, so no link between the two factors was claimed.
examples.cn: 这项研究得到零结果，因此没有宣称两个因素之间存在联系。

examples.en: Remember to check the variable for null before using it.
examples.cn: 在使用该变量之前，记得检查它是否为空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「难了」——合同被划掉，说「难了」，彻底作废；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ne（不）+ ullus（任何一个）→ nullus（一个也没有；零）→ 法律拉丁语「无效的」→ 英语 null。同族有 nullify、nullity、annul，核心义是「无、不存在」。

sensesIntro.en: From the Latin word for none, null branches into law, value, mathematics, statistics, and computing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拉丁语表示「无」的词出发，null 分出法律、价值、数学、统计与计算机几条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped contract crossed out in red until the page is blank.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖了章的合同被红笔划掉，整页变成空白。

branches.en: THE LAW: a document with no force is the oldest and strongest sense.
branches.cn: 法律线：没有效力的文书，是最古老也最牢固的义项。

branches.en: THE VALUE: votes and effort count for nothing, so they are null too.
branches.cn: 价值线：选票与努力也变得一文不值，于是同样称 null。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: zero in mathematics becomes no effect in statistics.
branches.cn: 数字线：数学里的零，在统计学里变成「没有效应」。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: a field holding nothing gets its own digital value.
branches.cn: 机器线：什么都不装的字段获得了自己的数字取值。

branches.en: THE FORMULA: the legal doublet keeps the Latin word forever paired with its French twin.
branches.cn: 套语线：法律双式短语让拉丁词永远与法语同义词配对。

intro.en: Null is a bare Latin stem that English rarely uses alone, yet it supports a whole family of formal words.
intro.cn: null 是一个裸拉丁词干，英语很少单独使用它，它却撑起了一整族正式用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nullus, ne, and ullus are recorded; nullus is the fused negative of ne plus ullus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nullus、ne、ullus 均有记录；nullus 是 ne 与 ullus 融合后的否定形式。

items.example: Ne is the first half of nullus.
items.exampleCN: ne 是 nullus 的前半部分。

items.example: Ullus is the any that ne cancels.
items.exampleCN: ullus 就是被 ne 否定的「任何一个」。

items.example: Nullus is the direct source of null.
items.exampleCN: nullus 是 null 的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ify forms nullify, to make void.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 构成 nullify，义为「使作废」。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms nullity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 nullity。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms nullification.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 nullification。

items.example: Null is used mainly in law and technology.
items.exampleCN: null 主要用于法律与技术语境。

items.example: Null and void is the standard legal doublet.
items.exampleCN: null and void 是标准的法律双式短语。

items.example: Nullify is the everyday verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: nullify 是这个词族里最常用的动词。

definition_zh: 计数；计数法；数制
definition_en: the act or system of counting and naming numbers
core_image: 一个孩子在石门框前一划一划地数石头，每一块都叫得出名字
scene: 考古队在遗址里数石刻记号，想知道先民怎样记账。The archaeologists studied the ancient numeration to see how early farmers counted their grain.
sceneCN: 这里 numeration 指「计数法，即一套数数并给数命名的体系」（第 2 个义项：计数法、记数体系）；句意是考古学家研究古代计数法，想弄清早期农民怎样清点谷物。

pos.zh: 计数；计数法；记数体系；数制

derivatives.zh: 动词，由名词 numeration 反推的词干 + -ate 构成，义为「计数；数数」
同出拉丁词根 numerus（数），加 -al 构成，义为「数字的；用数字表示的」
同出 numerus，-al 名词化，义为「数字；数词」，指书写符号而非整套体系
in-（不）+ numerare（计数）+-able（可……的），义为「数不清的」
en-（使进入）+ numer 数 + -ate，义为「逐项列举；清点」

senses.title: The act of counting
senses.definition: the act of counting things one by one to find how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 把事物一件一件数过去，以确定数量的动作
senses.example: The census began with a slow numeration of every household.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查从逐户慢慢清点开始。
senses.why: Latin numerare means to count, and the suffix -ion turns that action into the noun for the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 numerare 就是「数」，后缀 -ion 把这个动作变成名词，于是就是清点这件事本身。

senses.title: A system of naming numbers
senses.definition: an organized way of naming and writing numbers, such as base ten
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地给数命名和书写的方式，例如十进制
senses.example: Roman numeration used letters where we now use figures.
senses.exampleCN: 罗马计数法用字母，而我们现在用数字符号。
senses.why: Once counting is regular enough to teach and reuse, it hardens into a system, and the course noun names that whole method.
senses.whyCN: 计数一旦变得规范、可以教授和重复使用，就会固定成一套体系，这个词就指整套方法。

senses.title: A number base or place system
senses.definition: the arrangement of place values and base used to write numbers
senses.definitionCN: 书写数字时所用的数位排列与基底
senses.example: Base sixty numeration survives in our minutes and degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 六十进制计数法仍残留在分和度的写法里。
senses.why: Place value is the technical heart of a system, so the word often points at the base and places rather than at counting itself.
senses.whyCN: 位值是计数体系的技术核心，所以这个词常指向基底与数位，而不只是数数的动作。

senses.title: Enumeration in speech or writing
senses.definition: the setting out of items one after another in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在口头或书面中把各项事物依次列出
senses.example: His numeration of the charges took the judge half a morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他逐条陈述指控，花了法官半个上午。
senses.why: If counting is naming each item in turn, reading a list aloud is a kind of counting, and the word borrows that motion.
senses.whyCN: 既然计数就是依次叫出每一项，那么把清单念出来也是一种数，这个词就把这种节奏借了过来。

senses.title: Counting out money in church use
senses.titleCN: 旧用法：教会里的数钱仪式
senses.definition: an old church term for the formal counting of coins before parishioners
senses.definitionCN: 旧时教会用语，指当着信徒的面正式清点捐款硬币
senses.example: The old vestry records mention a solemn numeration after Sunday service.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的教区记录提到星期天礼拜后有一场庄重的数钱程序。
senses.why: Church records borrowed the plain Latin noun and kept the narrow scene of counting coins publicly.
senses.whyCN: 教会文书直接借用这个朴素的拉丁名词，保留了当众清点硬币的具体场景。

senses.title: A figure given in a count
senses.definition: a number reached by counting, especially in older arithmetic books
senses.definitionCN: 清点后得到的那个数目，多见于旧算术书
senses.example: The old arithmetic book called the final sum the total numeration.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧算术书把最后的和叫作总数。
senses.why: Old textbooks used a noun for the action also for the result it produced, a common drift from process to product.
senses.whyCN: 旧教科书常常用动作名词指它产生的结果，这是从过程漂移到成果的常见用法。

senses.title: Numbering as a property of populations
senses.definition: the official counting of a population or set of items for records
senses.definitionCN: 为建档而对人口或一批事物所做的官方清点
senses.example: Modern numeration of births now relies on national registers.
senses.exampleCN: 如今对出生人数的统计计数依靠国家登记册。
senses.why: Governments turned everyday counting into administration, so the noun now names large official counts.
senses.whyCN: 政府把日常的数数变成行政工作，这个词于是也指大规模的官方统计。

senses.title: A philosophy of countable reality
senses.titleCN: 抽象：以数为本的世界观
senses.definition: a theory that number is the basic substance of reality, associated with Pythagoras
senses.definitionCN: 认为数是实在之根本的理论，与毕达哥拉斯相关
senses.example: Pythagorean numeration held that all things are numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 毕达哥拉斯派的数论认为万物皆数。
senses.why: The ancient idea that reality is countable is the most abstract extension of a word that began with counting pebbles.
senses.whyCN: 「现实可以被数清」这一古老观念，是这个词从数石子一路走到最抽象处的结果。

intro.en: Numeration comes from Latin numeratio, the noun of numerare, to count, itself from numerus, a number.
intro.cn: numeration 源自拉丁语 numeratio，是动词 numerare（计数）的名词形式，再上溯到 numerus（数）。

items.en: Numerus meant a number, a count, or a portion.
items.cn: numerus 意为数、计数，也可指份额。

items.en: Numerare meant to count or to reckon, built on the noun.
items.cn: numerare 意为计数、核算，由这个名词派生。

items.en: Numeratio is the action noun, the act of counting or a reckoning.
items.cn: numeratio 是动作名词，指清点或核算之事。

items.en: The French form numératïon carried the noun into the mathematical schools.
items.cn: 法语形式 numératïon 把这个名词带入数学学派。

items.en: English adopted numeration first for the act of counting and numbering.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪先以 numeration 表示计数与编号的动作。

items.en: Modern mathematics gives the word to number bases, and statistics to population counts.
items.cn: 现代数学用它指记数制，统计学用它指人口清点。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root for number and is easily confused; the second group names acts and systems of counting.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「数」的拉丁词根，很容易混淆；第二组是计数动作与计数体系附近的词。

entries.definition: a written sign for a number, such as a figure or a letter used as a figure
entries.definitionCN: 表示数的书写符号，如阿拉伯数字或用字母充当的数符

entries.definition: expressed in or relating to numbers
entries.definitionCN: 用数字表示的；与数字有关的

entries.definition: to name things one by one in a list
entries.definitionCN: 逐项列出；列举

entries.definition: the simple act of finding how many things there are
entries.definitionCN: 找出若干事物共有多少个的简单动作

entries.definition: a set of written symbols used to record numbers or other values
entries.definitionCN: 记录数字或其他量值的书写符号系统

entries.definition: the branch of mathematics dealing with numbers and their operations
entries.definitionCN: 研究数与运算的数学分支

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb numerare, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词 numerare、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: numerus means number, and -ation marks an action or system, so numeration is the doing of numbers.
normal.cn: numerus 是「数」，-ation 表示动作或体系，所以 numeration 就是「数数这件事」。

normal.en: The family runs numeral, numerical, enumerate and innumerable, all from the same root.
normal.cn: 同族词 numeral、numerical、enumerate、innumerable 都出自同一词根。

normal.en: Decimal numeration simply means counting in tens.
normal.cn: 「十进制计数法」不过是按十来数数。

normal.en: To enumerate is to count items out loud one by one.
normal.cn: enumerate 就是把事物逐个念出来数一遍。

normal.en: Compare counting and numeration: counting is the act, numeration is the system behind it.
normal.cn: 对比 counting 与 numeration：前者是动作，后者是动作背后的体系。

abstract.en: Picture a hand dropping pebbles into a row, each stone given its own call.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把石子一颗颗排成一行，每颗石子都有一个叫法。

abstract.en: Think of a column of figures where each place holds ten times the place on its right.
abstract.cn: 想一排数位，每个位都装着右邻位的十倍。

abstract.en: Imagine a clerk reading a long list aloud, one name at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一名办事员把长长的名单一次一个名字念出来。

examples.en: Children learn decimal numeration before they learn to carry.
examples.cn: 孩子们先学会十进制计数法，再学进位。

examples.en: The museum displays tablets that record the numeration of temple offerings.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出的泥板记录着神庙供品的清点。

examples.en: His numeration of the errors made the report seem even worse.
examples.cn: 他把错误逐条列出来，让报告显得更加糟糕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛没来，先数牛」——牧场主数来数去，把清点和记数都叫 numeration；这只是联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 numerus（数）→ numerare（计数）→ numeratio（清点之事）→ 法语 numératïon → 英语 numeration，核心义「一五一十地数」。

sensesIntro.en: Numeration starts as the act of counting, grows into the system that organizes counting, and drifts to listing, official counts and abstract theories of number.
sensesIntro.cn: numeration 先指数数的动作，再指出数数组织成的体系，最后扩展到列举、官方清点与以数为本的理论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand moving along a row of pebbles, giving each one a name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手沿着一排石子移动，给每一颗一个叫法。

branches.en: The plain act of counting is the everyday core.
branches.cn: 朴素地清点事物，是这个词最日常的核心。

branches.en: Counting that is regular enough becomes a method with places and a base.
branches.cn: 计数一旦规律化，就成了带数位和基底的整套方法。

branches.en: Naming items one by one turns counting into listing.
branches.cn: 把各项依次点名，就让数数变成了列举。

branches.en: Older records name a public coin count and the sum it produces.
branches.cn: 旧文献既指当众数钱，也指数出来的那个数目。

branches.en: Official counts and Pythagorean theory both take the whole world as countable.
branches.cn: 官方统计与毕达哥拉斯理论都把整个世界看作可数的。

intro.en: Numeration is built on the Latin root numer, with the noun suffix -ation naming an action or system.
intro.cn: numeration 建立在拉丁词根 numer 上，名词后缀 -ation 表示动作或体系。

latinIntro.en: Latin numerare means to count, and numeratio names the act of counting.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 numerare 意为计数，numeratio 指清点这件事。

items.example: The root numer- appears in numeral and numeration.
items.exampleCN: 词根 numer- 出现在 numeral 与 numeration 中。

items.example: Numerus is the noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: numerus 是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: Numerare describes the counting hand.
items.exampleCN: numerare 描述那只数数的手。

items.example: The suffix -ation turns numerare into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 把 numerare 变成名词。

items.example: The suffix -al forms numeral and numerical.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 numeral 与 numerical。

items.example: The prefix en- helps form enumerate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 参与构成 enumerate。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms the verbs numerate and enumerate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成动词 numerate 与 enumerate。

items.example: The prefix in- helps form innumerable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 参与构成 innumerable。

items.example: The suffix -able forms innumerable and numerable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 innumerable 与 numerable。

definition_zh: 养育；培育；扶植；教养；(天性以外后天)养育环境
definition_en: to care for someone or something and help it grow and develop
core_image: 母亲俯身给幼芽浇水，一手托着苗，一手挡风
scene: 父母每天陪孩子读书、种菜、学规矩，希望孩子慢慢长大。Good parents nurture their children with patience and warmth.
sceneCN: 这里 nurture 指「用耐心和关爱养育、培育孩子成长」（第 1 个义项：抚养、养育）；句意是好父母用耐心和关爱养育自己的孩子。

pos.zh: 养育；培育；扶植；培养（感情、人才、事业）
养育；培养；教养；（相对「天性」而言的）养育环境

collocations.zh: 天性与养育（先天与后天）

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 作形容词，义为「有养育作用的；体贴关爱的」
同出古法语 norrir（抚养），义为「滋养；养大」，偏重供给养分
动词 nurture 加 -ance 构成，义为「养育行为；关爱照顾」，多为心理学术语
动词加 -er 构成，义为「养育者；照料人」

senses.title: To care for and bring up a child
senses.definition: to care for a child and help it grow up, especially with affection
senses.definitionCN: 带着关爱照料孩子，帮助其长大成人
senses.example: Her grandmother nurtured her through a difficult childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖母在她艰难的童年里把她养育成人。
senses.why: The Old French verb meant to feed and rear; feeding a child until it grows is the seed of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词本意是喂养、抚育；把孩子喂大、养大，是后来所有义项的种子。

senses.title: To encourage growth in plants or animals
senses.definition: to look after growing plants or animals so that they develop well
senses.definitionCN: 照看正在生长的动植物，使其发育良好
senses.example: He nurtured a row of seedlings on the kitchen windowsill.
senses.exampleCN: 他在厨房窗台上培育了一排幼苗。
senses.why: The literal feeding sense shifts easily from people to plants, where care is water and light.
senses.whyCN: 字面的「喂养」很容易从人转到植物身上，照料在那里就是水和光。

senses.title: To develop a skill or talent
senses.definition: to help a skill or talent grow through support and practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过支持与练习，让技能或才能逐步成长
senses.example: Good teachers nurture curiosity rather than test it away.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师培养好奇心，而不是把它考没了。
senses.why: A talent is a seed in a mind, and nurture treated as feeding turns into deliberate encouragement of ability.
senses.whyCN: 才能是头脑里的种子，把滋养理解为有意的供给，就生出「扶持能力成长」的用法。

senses.title: To keep something going over time
senses.titleCN: 扶植；维护（事业、感情、希望）
senses.definition: to keep a relationship, idea, ambition or hope alive with steady attention
senses.definitionCN: 用持续的投入让关系、理念、抱负或希望保持活力
senses.example: The couple nurtured their friendship across twenty years of distance.
senses.exampleCN: 这对朋友隔着二十年的距离，一直维护着他们的友谊。
senses.why: Anything that can wither needs care, so abstract things like hope and friendship also become objects of nurture.
senses.whyCN: 会枯萎的东西都需要照料，于是希望、友谊这些抽象之物也成了被养育的对象。

senses.title: The noun for upbringing
senses.titleCN: 养育（名词，指行为或过程）
senses.definition: the care and education given to someone, especially as a child
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人的照料与教育，尤指童年时期
senses.example: The boy was given a gentle nurture in the care of his aunt.
senses.exampleCN: 这个男孩在姑妈的照料下受到温和的养育。
senses.why: Every act noun turns the verb into a thing, so the feeding of a child becomes the noun nurture.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词总能把动词变成一件事，于是对孩子的喂养照料就成了名词 nurture。

senses.title: Environment as opposed to nature
senses.definition: the influence of upbringing and environment, contrasted with inherited nature
senses.definitionCN: 由成长经历与环境造成的影响，与遗传的天性相对
senses.example: Debate continues over whether nature or nurture shapes intelligence.
senses.exampleCN: 关于智力由天性还是由后天教养决定，争论仍在继续。
senses.why: The nursery scene is exactly what happens after birth, so nurture came to stand for the whole environmental side of a debate.
senses.whyCN: 育儿室里的场景正好是出生之后发生的事，因此 nurture 被用来代表争论中「环境」这一整面。

senses.title: Someone who cares for the young
senses.definition: an older use for a person who nurses or rears a child
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指哺育或抚养孩子的人
senses.example: The old poem calls the nurse a faithful nurture of the young.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古诗把保姆称作家里忠实的养育者。
senses.why: In earlier English the noun could name the person as well as the act, a trace of its feeding origin.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的英语里，这个名词既能指行为也能指人，这是它「喂养」出身留下的痕迹。

intro.en: Nurture comes through Old French noureture from nourriture, the noun of norrir, to nourish, from Latin nutrire.
intro.cn: nurture 经古法语 noureture 而来，出自 nourriture，即动词 norrir（滋养）的名词，再上溯到拉丁语 nutrire。

items.en: Nutrire meant to feed, to suckle, and so to bring up the young.
items.cn: nutrire 意为喂养、哺乳，因而有抚育幼仔之义。

items.en: The related noun nutrix means a nurse, one who feeds the child.
items.cn: 相关名词 nutrix 指乳母，即喂奶的人。

items.en: Norrir meant to nourish or rear, and nourriture named the feeding or upbringing.
items.cn: norrir 意为滋养、抚育，nourriture 指喂养或教养。

items.en: English took the word as norture or nurture, first naming the act of rearing a child.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪以 norture 或 nurture 借入，最初指抚养孩子的行为。

items.en: The spelling settles as nurture, and the word spreads to plants, skills and hopes.
items.cn: 拼写在十六世纪定为 nurture，用法扩展到植物、技能与希望。

items.en: Philosophy and psychology pair nurture with nature in debate over what shapes a person.
items.cn: 哲学与心理学把 nurture 与 nature 并提，讨论是什么塑造一个人。

note.en: The first group shares the feeding root and invites confusion; the second group holds the words for bringing something up.
note.cn: 第一组共享「喂养」这一词根，容易混淆；第二组是与「抚养、培养」同场的词。

entries.definition: to give what is needed for growth and health to a body
entries.definitionCN: 给身体提供成长与健康所需之物；与 nurture 同源

entries.definition: food or whatever keeps something alive and growing
entries.definitionCN: 食物，或任何维持生命与成长之物

entries.definition: a substance that living things take in from food in order to grow
entries.definitionCN: 生物从食物中摄取以成长的物质；与 nurture 同出拉丁 nutrire

entries.definition: to bring up a child, usually in everyday speech
entries.definitionCN: 把孩子养大，多为日常口语用法

entries.definition: to care for a child in a family that is not its own, or to encourage growth
entries.definitionCN: 在并非亲生父母的家庭中抚养孩子，或助长某事物发展

entries.definition: to prepare land and grow crops, or to develop a quality over time
entries.definitionCN: 耕作土地、种植作物，或长期培植某种品质

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb nutrire, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词 nutrire、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Nutrire is to feed, so nurture always keeps the image of food and care.
normal.cn: nutrire 就是喂食，所以 nurture 始终带着「供给」与「照料」的画面。

normal.en: Nutrient and nutrition share the root: what feeds the body feeds the mind too.
normal.cn: nutrient 与 nutrition 同根：喂饱身体的东西，也能喂饱头脑。

normal.en: Nature or nurture is the classic question of heredity against environment.
normal.cn: 「天性还是教养」是遗传与环境之争的经典问法。

normal.en: To nurture a talent is to water a seed until it opens.
normal.cn: 培养人才，就是给种子浇水，等它发芽。

normal.en: Compare nurture and nourish: nurture covers care and education, nourish mainly covers food.
normal.cn: 对比 nurture 与 nourish：前者涵盖照料与教育，后者主要是供给食物。

abstract.en: Picture a cupped hand shielding a small flame from wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拢起的手，替一小簇火苗挡风。

abstract.en: Think of a gardener who looses the soil before the seed is even planted.
abstract.cn: 想一位园丁，在种子还没下地时就先把土松好。

abstract.en: Imagine two copies of the same seed placed in soil and in stone.
abstract.cn: 想象同一颗种子的两份，一份放进泥土，一份搁在石头上。

examples.en: She nurtured her son interest in music with weekend concerts.
examples.cn: 她用周末音乐会来培养儿子对音乐的热爱。

examples.en: Rainforest soil is poor, yet it nurtures immense life.
examples.cn: 雨林的土壤很贫瘠，却养育着极其丰富的生命。

examples.en: The charity was set up to nurture young engineers.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构旨在培养年轻工程师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呐，chure 吃」——像妈妈蹲下来对孩子说「呐，再吃一口」，一口一口喂大，就是养育。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 nutrire（喂养、哺乳）→ 名词 nutrix（乳母）→ 古法语 norrir（滋养）与 nourriture（喂养）→ 中古英语 nurture，核心义「一口一口喂大」。

sensesIntro.en: Nurture begins with feeding a child, passes to plants, to abilities and relationships, and finally names the whole environment side of nature against nurture.
sensesIntro.cn: nurture 从喂养孩子开始，转到植物，再到能力与关系，最后指代「天性对教养」之争中的整个环境一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand cupped around a seedling, feeding it light and water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拢住幼苗，给它浇水和阳光。

branches.en: Rearing a child is the closest sense to the feeding origin.
branches.cn: 抚养孩子，是离「喂养」本义最近的义项。

branches.en: Caring for plants moves the act from people to living things without words.
branches.cn: 照料植物，把这一动作从人身上移到不会说话的生物上。

branches.en: Supporting a talent treats ability as something that can be watered.
branches.cn: 扶持才能，是把能力当成可以浇灌的东西。

branches.en: Keeping a relationship alive shows the care of nurture applied to abstract things.
branches.cn: 维护感情，显示养育之力被用到抽象事物上。

branches.en: The noun branch turns the act into upbringing, environment, and finally the caregiver.
branches.cn: 名词这一分支把动作变成教养、环境，最后指养育者本人。

intro.en: Nurture is built on the Latin root nutri, carried through Old French, with -ture naming what is done.
intro.cn: nurture 建立在拉丁词根 nutri 上，经古法语传来，词尾 -ture 表示所做之事。

latinIntro.en: Latin nutrire means to feed and rear, and nutrix names the one who nurses a child.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nutrire 意为喂养、抚育，nutrix 指乳母。

items.example: The root nutri- appears in nutritious and nutrition.
items.exampleCN: 词根 nutri- 出现在 nutritious 与 nutrition 中。

items.example: Nutrire is the feeding verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: nutrire 是整个词族背后的「喂养」动词。

items.example: Nutrix names the woman who feeds a baby.
items.exampleCN: nutrix 指给婴儿喂奶的妇女。

items.example: Norrir carries the Latin verb into French.
items.exampleCN: norrir 把拉丁动词带入法语。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ture makes nurture a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ture 让 nurture 成为动作名词。

items.meaning: doing, or having the quality of
items.meaningCN: 表示进行或具有该性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms nurturing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 nurturing。

items.example: The suffix -er forms nurturer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 nurturer。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或动作的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ance forms nurturance.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ance 构成 nurturance。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms nutritious from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 与同一词根构成 nutritious。

definition_zh: 有营养的；营养丰富的；滋养身体的
definition_en: full of the substances that a body needs in order to grow and stay healthy
core_image: 一碗热腾腾的杂粮粥，勺子舀起时看得见谷物和豆子
scene: 病后的老人需要吃好东西恢复体力。The doctor told her to eat vegetables every day because they are nutritious.
sceneCN: 这里 nutritious 指「富含身体所需的养分」（第 1 个义项：营养丰富、有营养）；句意是医生让她每天吃蔬菜，因为蔬菜营养丰富。

pos.zh: 有营养的；营养丰富的；滋养的

derivatives.zh: 同出拉丁 nutrire，加 -tion 构成，义为「营养；营养学」
名词 nutrition 加 -al 构成，义为「营养的；营养方面的」，常指成分表而非美味
同根 nutrit 加 -ent，义为「营养素；滋养的」
经古法语 norrir 同出一源，义为「滋养；供养」
mal-（坏、不足）+ nutrition，义为「营养不良」

senses.title: Rich in the nutrients a body needs
senses.definition: containing a good supply of the things a person or animal needs to stay healthy
senses.definitionCN: 含有供给人或动物维持健康所需的丰富养分
senses.example: Lentils and brown rice make a nutritious cheap meal.
senses.exampleCN: 扁豆配糙米就是一餐价廉而营养丰富的饭。
senses.why: Latin nutrire means to feed, and -ous adds fullness, so nutritious is literally feeding in quality to a high degree.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nutrire 是「喂养」，-ous 表示「充满」，所以 nutritious 字面就是「在喂养这一属性上很足」。

senses.title: Good for health in a general way
senses.definition: generally healthy to eat, even where the exact nutrients are not counted
senses.definitionCN: 泛指吃了对健康有好处，并不细究具体成分
senses.example: A bowl of hot soup in winter is both comforting and nutritious.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天一碗热汤既暖身又养人。
senses.why: Everyday speech loosens the strict chemical sense into a warm general approval of food that does you good.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把严格的化学含义放松成对「吃了有好处」的笼统赞许。

senses.title: Feeding growth in plants and soil
senses.definition: carrying the minerals and organic matter that help plants grow
senses.definitionCN: 含有帮助植物生长的矿物质与有机质
senses.example: The river silt leaves a nutritious layer over the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 河水带来的淤泥在田上留下一层肥沃的养分。
senses.why: If the root verb means to feed, then anything that feeds a growing thing, soil included, can be called nutritious.
senses.whyCN: 既然词根动词意为喂养，那么任何滋养生长之物，包括土壤，都能叫 nutritious。

senses.title: Full of value for the mind
senses.definition: figuratively, supplying ideas or experiences that enrich the mind
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义，提供丰富头脑的思想或经历
senses.example: She called the school library a nutritious place for young readers.
senses.exampleCN: 她称学校图书馆是让小读者长见识的养人之处。
senses.why: The feeding image extends from stomach to mind, the way books and music are said to nourish us.
senses.whyCN: 「喂食」的画面从胃延伸到头脑，正如书和音乐被说成能滋养我们。

senses.title: Promoting recovery in the sick
senses.definition: in medical writing, describing food chosen to help a patient recover or gain strength
senses.definitionCN: 医学文献中，形容为帮助病人康复或增重而选的食物
senses.example: Nurses prepared a nutritious broth for the patient after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士为术后病人准备了一锅营养的肉汤。
senses.why: Medicine picks up the word because recovery depends on feeding the body well, a literal echo of nutrire.
senses.whyCN: 医学采用这个词，是因为康复有赖于好好喂养身体，正好回响 nutrire 的本义。

senses.title: Desirable in food marketing
senses.definition: used in advertising to claim that a product is wholesome and full of goodness
senses.definitionCN: 广告词中用来宣称产品有益且富含养分
senses.example: The label called the cereal nutritious, but sugar came second.
senses.exampleCN: 标签说这款麦片营养丰富，可糖排在配料第二位。
senses.why: When the word sells, it can loosen from measured nutrients into a mere promise of wholesomeness.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词被用来推销时，它可能从可测量的养分滑落为空洞的「有益无害」承诺。

senses.title: Rich food that fattens the body
senses.definition: an older use for rich food that builds the body up quickly
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指能迅速把身体养壮的肥厚食物
senses.example: Old cookbooks praise eggs and cream as highly nutritious.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时菜谱把蛋和奶油称为极富营养之物。
senses.why: Before vitamins were known, nutritious meant simply the food that visibly made a person sturdier.
senses.whyCN: 在维生素被发现之前，nutritious 只指吃了明显让人更结实的东西。

intro.en: Nutritious comes from Latin nutricius, nourishing, formed on nutrix, a nurse, from nutrire, to feed.
intro.cn: nutritious 源自拉丁语 nutricius（有滋养作用的），由 nutrix（乳母）派生，而 nutrix 又出自 nutrire（喂养）。

items.en: Nutrire meant to feed, to suckle, and hence to rear young.
items.cn: nutrire 意为喂养、哺乳，因此也指抚育幼小。

items.en: Nutrix is the nurse, the person who feeds the child.
items.cn: nutrix 是乳母，即给孩子喂食的人。

items.en: Nutricius meant nourishing, of the kind that feeds and strengthens.
items.cn: nutricius 意为有滋养作用的，即能喂养和强健身体的那一类。

items.en: French kept several forms of the root in nourrir and nutrition, growing from the Latin source.
items.cn: 法语在 nourrir 与 nutrition 中保留了这一词根的多种形式，皆出自同一拉丁来源。

items.en: English adopted nutritious, first mainly in medical writing about food that strengthens.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 nutritious，最初多用于讨论食物强身的医学文献。

items.en: With modern nutrition science the word marks food rich in known nutrients.
items.cn: 随着现代营养学的发展，这个词专指标记着已知营养素的食物。

note.en: The first group shares the feeding root and is easily mixed with nutrition and nutritional; the second group holds words for food that does good.
note.cn: 第一组共享「喂养」词根，很容易与 nutrition、nutritional 混淆；第二组是与「有益食物」同场的词。

entries.definition: the process of getting food and the science that studies it
entries.definitionCN: 摄取食物的过程，以及研究它的科学；与 nutritious 同根，但是名词

entries.definition: relating to nutrition as a subject, as in a label listing contents
entries.definitionCN: 与营养学这一主题有关的，如列成分的标签

entries.definition: one particular substance a body needs, such as iron or vitamin C
entries.definitionCN: 身体所需的某一种特定物质，如铁或维生素

entries.definition: to feed and keep growing, a verb that hides the same Latin source
entries.definitionCN: 喂养并使其生长，这个动词藏着同一拉丁来源

entries.definition: good for the body and unlikely to cause illness
entries.definitionCN: 对身体有益的，不太会引发疾病

entries.definition: simple and clean food or activity that people believe is good for them
entries.definitionCN: 朴素干净的食物或活动，人们认为对自己有好处

entries.definition: having vitamins or minerals added on purpose during processing
entries.definitionCN: 加工时刻意添加了维生素或矿物质的

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb nutrire, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词 nutrire、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Nutri- means to feed and -ous means full of, so nutritious is full of feeding power.
normal.cn: nutri- 是喂养，-ous 是充满，所以 nutritious 就是「充满喂养之力」。

normal.en: The family runs nutrition, nutritional, nutrient and nourish, all from the same source.
normal.cn: 同族词 nutrition、nutritional、nutrient、nourish 都出自同一来源。

normal.en: A nutritious diet is a pattern of eating, while a nutrient is one single substance.
normal.cn: 有营养的饮食是一种吃法，而 nutrient 只是一种物质。

normal.en: Mal helps build malnutrition, the shortage of what is nutritious.
normal.cn: mal- 参与构成 malnutrition，即缺少有营养的东西。

normal.en: Compare nutritious and healthy: a food may be healthy in moderation yet not especially nutritious.
normal.cn: 对比 nutritious 与 healthy：某种食物适量吃可能有益，却未必营养丰富。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl of warm porridge where grains and beans can be seen swimming.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗热粥，里面浮着看得见的谷粒和豆子。

abstract.en: Think of a spoonful going straight to rebuilding muscle.
abstract.cn: 想一勺食物直接去修补肌肉。

abstract.en: Imagine good soil feeding a plant, then the plant feeding a person.
abstract.cn: 想肥沃的土养着植物，植物再养着人。

examples.en: Fresh fruit is a highly nutritious snack for children.
examples.cn: 新鲜水果是给孩子的高营养零食。

examples.en: The parents were advised to serve more nutritious meals at home.
examples.cn: 有人建议父母在家多准备些有营养的饭菜。

examples.en: He explained that cheap beans are as nutritious as expensive meat.
examples.cn: 他解释说便宜的豆子和贵肉一样有营养。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛吹舌头」——牛一边嚼草一边吹舌头，其实吃的是青草，青草营养丰富。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 nutrire（喂养）→ nutrix（乳母）→ nutricius（有滋养作用的）→ 英语 nutritious，核心义「能喂饱生命的」。

sensesIntro.en: Nutritious moves from the strict sense of full of nutrients to a loose sense of good for health, then to soil, to the mind, to clinical use and finally to marketing.
sensesIntro.cn: nutritious 从严格意义上的「富含营养素」，松散为「对健康有益」，再转到土壤、精神、临床用法，最后进入广告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steaming bowl of grain, each spoonful rebuilding the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一碗冒着热气的杂粮，每一勺都在修补身体。

branches.en: The measurable sense of rich in nutrients is the scientific centre.
branches.cn: 「富含营养素」这一可测量的含义，是这个词的科学中心。

branches.en: Everyday talk and clinical advice both loosen the word into simply good for you.
branches.cn: 日常说法与临床建议都把它松弛成笼统的「对身体好」。

branches.en: Soil and silt carry the word from the table to the field.
branches.cn: 土壤与淤泥把这个词从餐桌带到田里。

branches.en: Feeding the mind is the metaphorical extension of feeding the body.
branches.cn: 喂养头脑，是喂养身体这一意象的比喻延伸。

branches.en: Marketing and old cookbooks show the word drifting from fact to promise.
branches.cn: 广告与旧菜谱显示这个词从事实漂向承诺。

intro.en: Nutritious is built on the Latin root nutri, with -ous marking fullness of quality.
intro.cn: nutritious 建立在拉丁词根 nutri 上，词尾 -ous 表示「充满某种性质」。

latinIntro.en: Latin nutrire means to feed; nutrix is the nurse, and nutricius means nourishing.
