latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nutrire 意为喂养，nutrix 指乳母，nutricius 意为有滋养作用的。

items.example: The root nutri- appears in nutritious and nutrition.
items.exampleCN: 词根 nutri- 出现在 nutritious 与 nutrition 中。

items.example: Nutrire is the verb at the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: nutrire 是这个词族最底层的动词。

items.example: Nutrix is the nurse who feeds the baby.
items.exampleCN: nutrix 就是给婴儿喂奶的乳母。

items.example: Nutricius is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: nutricius 是这个英语形容词的直接来源。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous marks fullness in nutritious.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 在 nutritious 中表示「充满」。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -tion forms nutrition.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 构成 nutrition。

items.example: The suffix -al forms nutritional.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 nutritional。

items.meaningCN: 表示进行或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ent forms nutrient.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 构成 nutrient。

items.example: The prefix mal- forms malnutrition.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mal- 构成 malnutrition。

definition_zh: 橡树；栎树；橡木；橡木家具（不可数）；橡树木材制成的
definition_en: a large tree with hard wood and seeds called acorns, or the hard wood of that tree
core_image: 林地里一棵枝干粗壮的老橡树，树下落着几颗橡果
scene: 秋日的林地小路上，一位老人停在古橡树下，抬头望着密密的树冠。On the autumn woodland path, an old man stopped under the ancient oak and looked up at the dense crown.
sceneCN: 这里 oak 是「橡树」（第 1 个义项：结橡果的硬木大乔木）；句意：秋日的林地小路上，一位老人停在古橡树下，抬头望着密密的树冠。

pos.zh: 橡树；栎树；橡木；橡木家具

derivatives.zh: oak 加形容词后缀 -en（材料后缀），义为「橡木制的」，属书面语
oak 加 land（土地）构成的复合词，义为「橡树林地」，多作地名
oak 加 wood（木材）构成的复合词，义为「橡木；橡木林」
oak 加指小后缀 -let，义为「小橡树」，属少见词

senses.title: A large hard-wooded tree
senses.definition: a large tree with a tough bark, lobed leaves and acorns as its fruit
senses.definitionCN: 一种树皮粗糙、叶缘呈波浪裂片、果实为橡果的大树
senses.example: An oak stands at the centre of the village green.
senses.exampleCN: 村中绿地的中央立着一棵橡树。
senses.why: The tree sense is the source of the whole word, and acorn literally means the fruit of the oak.
senses.whyCN: 树本身是这个词的来源，古英语里橡果一词的字面意思就是「橡树的果实」，可见树是该词最初的形象。

senses.title: The wood of this tree
senses.definition: the hard, heavy and durable wood obtained from an oak tree
senses.definitionCN: 从橡树上取得的坚硬、沉重且耐用的木材
senses.example: The staircase is made of dark oak.
senses.exampleCN: 这道楼梯是用深色橡木做的。
senses.why: The second sense is simply the tree turned into material, because oak wood is famously hard and long-lasting.
senses.whyCN: 树被砍下就成了材料；橡木以坚硬耐久著称，于是树名直接转指这种木材。

senses.title: Furniture or fittings made of oak
senses.definition: furniture, doors or fittings that are made of oak wood
senses.definitionCN: 用橡木制成的家具、门或门窗等装修部件
senses.example: The old pub is full of dark oaks and brass taps.
senses.exampleCN: 这家老酒馆里满是深色橡木家具和黄铜龙头。
senses.why: When the material becomes the main visible feature, the word slides from the wood to the objects built from it.
senses.whyCN: 当橡木成了物件最显眼的材质时，词义就从木材滑向了用木材做成的东西，这是材料词语常见的转指。

senses.title: Used to describe oak things
senses.definition: made of oak wood, usually used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 用橡木做成的，通常放在名词前作定语
senses.example: She opened the heavy oak door with both hands.
senses.exampleCN: 她用双手推开了那扇沉重的橡木门。
senses.why: The material noun works as a pre-noun modifier in English, so oak becomes a simple adjective in phrases like an oak door.
senses.whyCN: 英语里材料名词可以直接放在名词前充当修饰语，于是 oak 在「橡木门」这类短语里就成了形容词性的定语。

senses.title: A symbol of strength or age
senses.definition: used in images and expressions to suggest strength, steadiness or long life
senses.definitionCN: 在比喻和固定表达里象征强健、沉稳或长寿
senses.example: His old oak of a grandfather still walks three miles a day.
senses.exampleCN: 他那像老橡树一样硬朗的祖父每天还走三英里。
senses.why: Oaks live for centuries and stand through storms, so the image of the tree naturally grew into a metaphor for a strong, sturdy person.
senses.whyCN: 橡树能活上几百年，又能挺过风暴，树的形象自然引申为「强壮、结实的人」，这是由树木生命力衍生出的比喻义。

senses.title: The oak leaf as a national emblem
senses.definition: the leaf or spray of oak used as an emblem on coins, medals and national badges
senses.definitionCN: 用作硬币、奖章或国家徽记图案的橡叶或橡树枝
senses.example: A small oak leaf appears on the national emblem.
senses.exampleCN: 国徽上有一片小小的橡叶。
senses.why: Because the oak symbolised strength, the Germanic states adopted its leaves for coins and national emblems, and English kept that usage.
senses.whyCN: 橡树象征着力量，日耳曼诸邦便用橡叶装饰硬币与国徽，英语沿用下来，于是 oak 又指这种图案本身。

senses.title: An oak-like plant in another family
senses.titleCN: （植物名中）借橡树之名的植物
senses.definition: a plant whose name contains oak because its leaves or habit resemble those of a real oak
senses.definitionCN: 因叶片或生长形态像橡树而以 oak 命名的植物，并非真正的栎属植物
senses.example: The poison oak by the trail can cause an itchy rash.
senses.exampleCN: 小路边一株毒橡树可能导致皮肤发痒起疹。
senses.why: Botanists and settlers named other plants after the oak when their leaves or shape looked alike, extending the name through resemblance.
senses.whyCN: 植物学家和移民看到别的植物叶片或形态像橡树，就用橡树之名去命名，这是典型的「依相似而扩展名称」。

intro.en: Oak is one of the oldest tree names in English, coming from Old English ac, which also supplied acorn, the fruit of the oak.
intro.cn: oak 是英语里最古老的树名之一，来自古英语 ac；古英语里的「橡果」一词 acorn 正是由 ac 加表示果实的名词词尾构成的。

items.en: The reconstructed form aiks names the oak, a tree heavy with timber value.
items.cn: 重构形式 aiks 指橡树，是一种木材价值很高的树。

items.en: The word appears as ac, the name of the oak and the base of acorn.
items.cn: 古英语写作 ac，既是橡树之名，也是 acorn 的词根。

items.en: The spelling settles into ok, ooke and oke, and the meaning widens to oak wood.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 ok、ooke、oke 等，词义也从树扩大到橡木。

items.en: Oak becomes the standard form and the typical timber of ships, churches and furniture in England.
items.cn: oak 成为标准拼写，并成为英国造船、建教堂、打家具的典型木材。

items.en: The word keeps the tree, the timber and the emblem, and forms place names such as Oakland and Oakham.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了树、木材和徽记三层含义，并用它构成 Oakland、Oakham 一类的地名。

note.en: Oak belongs to the tree family around Old English ac, while its near meanings are the other hard timbers and the words for the tree itself.
note.cn: oak 属于古英语 ac 这一树名词族；它的近义一侧则是其他硬木与表示树木的名词。

entries.definition: the nut of the oak tree
entries.definitionCN: 橡果，由古英语 ac（橡树）构成，与 oak 同源

entries.definition: made of oak wood
entries.definitionCN: 橡木制的，由 oak 加后缀 -en 构成

entries.definition: land covered with oak trees
entries.definitionCN: 橡树林地，由 oak 与 land 构成，多见于地名

entries.definition: a nonstandard spelling that is not an English word
entries.definitionCN: 非标准拼法，英语中并无此词，与 oak 只是字形相近

entries.definition: a large tree with smooth grey bark and hard wood
entries.definitionCN: 山毛榉，也是树皮光滑、木质坚硬的秋天落叶大乔木

entries.definition: a tall tree with rough leaves and tough wood
entries.definitionCN: 榆树，高大、木材坚韧的落叶乔木

entries.definition: a forest tree with hard light-coloured wood
entries.definitionCN: 白蜡树，木质坚硬、颜色浅的林木

entries.definition: wood prepared for use in building
entries.definitionCN: 建筑用木材，oak 作为材料时的上位词

normalIntro.en: Oak is a tree that gives its name to its own fruit and its own timber, so one word covers the tree, the wood and the furniture.
normalIntro.cn: oak 是一种把自己的果实和木材都命名的树：一个词同时覆盖树、木材与家具。

normal.en: An acorn is literally the fruit of the oak, and the two words share an Old English root.
normal.cn: 橡果一词的字面意思就是「橡树的果实」，它与 oak 共享古英语词根。

normal.en: Say oak tree for the living plant, and just oak for the wood or the furniture.
normal.cn: 活着的植物说 oak tree，木材或家具只说 oak。

normal.en: An oak door, an oak floor and an oak table all use oak as a modifier.
normal.cn: 橡木门、橡木地板、橡木桌里，oak 都作定语修饰。

normal.en: Old English ac had the plural acas, and later English made a plain plural oaks.
normal.cn: 古英语 ac 的复数是 acas，后来英语才形成规则的复数 oaks。

normal.en: Compare beech, elm and ash: all are hard white or brown timbers that name both tree and wood.
normal.cn: 对比 beech、elm 与 ash：它们都是硬质浅色或褐色木材，也都同时指树与木材。

abstract.en: Picture a huge oak with a spiky crown and a dozen acorns on the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵枝冠参差的大橡树，树下草地上躺着十几颗橡果。

abstract.en: Imagine sawing a plank from the log and watching the gold wood appear.
abstract.cn: 想象从原木上锯下一块木板，金黄木纹慢慢露出来。

abstract.en: Think of a century-old oak still standing after a storm has broken the younger trees.
abstract.cn: 想象一场风暴折断了年轻的小树，而百年老橡树依旧挺立。

examples.en: The oak in the churchyard is over three hundred years old.
examples.cn: 教堂墓地里的那棵橡树已经三百多年了。

examples.en: The table is made of pale oak and smells faintly of wax.
examples.cn: 这张桌子是浅色橡木做的，还带一点蜡的味道。

examples.en: Squirrels bury acorns from the oaks across the park.
examples.cn: 松鼠把公园各处橡树的橡果埋起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧克」——听到橡树“OK，我来遮阴”，于是 ouk 近似 oak，代表那棵撑开枝叶的老橡树；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ac（橡树）→ 中古英语 ok/ooke → 英语 oak；古英语 ac + 名词词尾 -ern 构成 acorn（橡果），可见「橡树」是这一词族的根义。

sensesIntro.en: Oak starts with the living tree, passes to its timber and the furniture made from it, then extends into an adjective, a symbol of strength and a national emblem.
sensesIntro.cn: oak 先从活的树出发，转指木材和用木材做成的家具，再扩展为形容词、力量与长寿的象征以及国徽图案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stout old oak whose acorns litter the ground beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵粗壮的老橡树，橡果散落在树下的地面上。

branches.en: The living tree is the original and basic sense.
branches.cn: 活着的橡树是最原始、最基本的义项。

branches.en: The timber sense keeps only the material left after the tree is felled.
branches.cn: 木材义项只保留树被伐倒后剩下的材料。

branches.en: Furniture and the adjective both work from the material sense, one as a noun and one as a modifier.
branches.cn: 家具义项和形容词义项都由材料义发展而来，一为名词，一为定语。

branches.en: Strength and the national emblem both use the tree as a symbol rather than a thing.
branches.cn: 力量象征与国徽图案都把橡树当作象征，而不是实物。

branches.en: Plants with oak-like leaves borrow the name through resemblance to the real tree.
branches.cn: 叶片像橡树的植物借名而来，靠的是与真橡树的相似。

intro.en: Oak is a very old Germanic word with no Latin prefix or suffix of its own; its family grows through Old English compounds and English -en and -let.
intro.cn: oak 是很古老的日耳曼词，本身不含拉丁词缀；它的词族靠古英语复合词与英语后缀 -en、-let 扩展而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin names the oak as quercus, a word that is not related to English oak, but botanists still use it in scientific names.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把橡树叫 quercus，与英语 oak 并不同源，但植物学家至今把橡属写作 Quercus。

items.example: Old English ac is the direct ancestor of oak.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 ac 是 oak 的直接祖先。

items.example: Acorn joins ac with a noun ending meaning fruit.
items.exampleCN: acorn 由 ac 与表示果实的名词词尾组合而成。

items.example: Oak names both the tree and the wood.
items.exampleCN: oak 同时指树与木材。

items.example: The plural oaks marks more than one tree.
items.exampleCN: 复数 oaks 表示不止一棵橡树。

items.example: The suffix -en forms oaken.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -en 构成 oaken。

items.example: Oaken describes an old chest in a story.
items.exampleCN: oaken 在故事里形容一只旧木箱。

items.example: Oakland combines oak with land.
items.exampleCN: oakland 由 oak 与 land 组成。

items.example: The rare word oaklet uses -let for a small oak.
items.exampleCN: 少见的 oaklet 用 -let 表示小橡树。

items.example: Oak-leaved names plants by the shape of their leaves.
items.exampleCN: oak-leaved 按叶形给植物命名。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 橡树，与英语 oak 不同源
latinEntries.example: Quercus robur is the scientific name of the English oak.
latinEntries.exampleCN: Quercus robur 是英国橡树的学名。
robur 也是英语 robust 的来源。

definition_zh: 燕麦；燕麦植株；燕麦粒（成群）；燕麦粥；燕麦饲料
definition_en: a cereal plant grown for its grain in cool climates, or its grain, used as food for people and animals
core_image: 风吹过成片的燕麦田，细软的穗子在风里一起低头
scene: 清晨的农场上，马夫把一碗喷香的燕麦倒进马槽，马立刻伸过头来。On the farm at dawn, the stable hand poured a bowl of warm oat into the trough and the horse reached over at once.
sceneCN: 这里 oat 是「燕麦」（第 1 个义项：供人与牲畜食用的谷物），此处按英国英语用法以单数指这种谷物；句意：清晨的农场上，马夫把一碗喷香的燕麦倒进马槽，马立刻伸过头来。

derivatives.zh: oat 与 meal（磨碎的谷粉）构成的复合词，义为「燕麦粉；燕麦片」，美式英语里也指燕麦粥
oat 加形容词后缀 -en（材料后缀），义为「燕麦做的」，多见于旧式书面语
oat 加形容词后缀 -y，义为「有燕麦味的」，属少见的口语用法
oat 与 wild（野生的）构成的短语，指野生燕麦：既是田间杂草，也见于「年轻时放纵」的习语

senses.title: The grain and its plant
senses.definition: a cereal plant grown in cool climates, or the grain it produces
senses.definitionCN: 在凉爽气候中种植的谷物，及其结出的谷粒
senses.example: Farmers in the north grow oat and barley side by side.
senses.exampleCN: 北方的农民把燕麦和大麦种在一起。
senses.why: The grain is the original sense, and English can use the singular oat for the mass of grain in British usage.
senses.whyCN: 谷粒义是最初的本义；英国英语里可以用单数 oat 指这种谷物的总体，就像用 wheat 那样。

senses.title: Cereal plants or crops in the field
senses.definition: the plants growing in the field, usually counted with the plural
senses.definitionCN: 长在田里的植株，通常用复数形式计数
senses.example: He sowed the oats in April and watched them sprout.
senses.exampleCN: 他四月播下燕麦，看着它们发芽。
senses.why: When speakers point at growing plants they count them, so the plural oats takes over the field sense.
senses.whyCN: 指田里一株株生长的植株时，人们会数个数，所以复数 oats 承担了田间作物的义项。

senses.title: Oatmeal served as porridge
senses.definition: grains of oat cooked in water or milk into a soft hot cereal
senses.definitionCN: 把燕麦加水或牛奶煮成的软热粥
senses.example: He has a bowl of oats with honey every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上吃一碗加蜂蜜的燕麦粥。
senses.why: The grain cooked into a dish is still called by its grain name, so oats slides from raw food to breakfast.
senses.whyCN: 谷物煮熟后仍用谷名来称呼，于是 oats 从原料滑向了早餐主食。

senses.title: Horse feed
senses.definition: the grain given to horses and other farm animals as a feed
senses.definitionCN: 用来喂马和其他牲畜的燕麦饲料
senses.example: The stable boy poured a bucket of oats into the manger.
senses.exampleCN: 马夫把一桶燕麦倒进马槽。
senses.why: Oats have been horse feed for centuries, and this use keeps the grain sense but changes the eater.
senses.whyCN: 几百年来燕麦一直是马的饲料，这个义项保留了「谷粒」的本义，只是吃它的对象从人变成了牲畜。

senses.title: Used before a noun
senses.definition: used before another noun to show that something is made from or contains oats
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，表示某物由燕麦制成或含有燕麦
senses.example: She drinks oat milk in her coffee every day.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天在咖啡里加燕麦奶。
senses.why: English lets a food noun modify a following noun, so oat became a modifier in oat milk, oat bread and oat fibre.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许食物名词直接修饰后面的名词，于是 oat 在燕麦奶、燕麦面包、燕麦纤维里变成了定语。

senses.title: In idioms of youthful energy
senses.definition: in phrases such as sow wild oats, the word images the grain of wild grasses and youthful wildness
senses.definitionCN: 在 sow wild oats 一类习语中，借野燕麦的形象表示年轻时放纵、胡闹
senses.example: He is busy living down the wild oats he sowed in his youth.
senses.exampleCN: 他正忙着为年轻时纵情胡闹的行为收拾名声。
senses.why: Wild oats were a useless weed, so sowing them became a picture of wasting youthful energy on wild behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 野燕麦是没用的杂草，种野燕麦就成了「把青春精力耗在放纵行为上」的画面，习语由此而来。

intro.en: Oat comes from Old English ate, probably with the help of Old Norse, and its earlier form is only known as a reconstruction.
intro.cn: oat 来自古英语 ate，可能还受到古诺斯语影响；更早的词形目前只见于重构形式。

items.en: The reconstructed noun aitan describes a wild grain related to oat.
items.cn: 重构名词 aitan 指一种与燕麦相近的野生谷物，属重构形式。

items.en: The grain is recorded as ate, written in fields and food texts.
items.cn: 古英语把这种谷物记作 ate，见于农事与食物文字。

items.en: The Scandinavian form contributes to the later English word, a borrowing that is generally accepted.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚形式也对后来的英语词形有贡献，这一借入关系一般认为成立。

items.en: The word settles as ote and then oote, and the plural otes becomes common.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 ote、oote，复数 otes 也开始常见。

items.en: The modern spelling oats takes shape, and oatmeal and oat porridge spread from Scotland and the north.
items.cn: 现代拼写 oats 成形，燕麦粥与燕麦片从苏格兰和英格兰北部传向各地。

items.en: The word becomes a food label as oat milk and oat fibre enter everyday shopping.
items.cn: 随着燕麦奶与燕麦纤维进入日常消费，这个词也成了食品标签上的用词。

note.en: Oat is a cereal word whose near meanings are the other grains and whose look-alikes are its compounds and a near-spelling.
note.cn: oat 是谷物词，形近一侧是它的复合词与一个近似拼写，近义一侧则是其他谷物。

entries.definition: the plural of oat, used as a mass food noun
entries.definitionCN: oat 的复数，常作不可数食物名词使用

entries.definition: crushed oats, or a porridge made from them
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦片、燕麦粉，或燕麦粥，由 oat 与 meal 构成

entries.definition: made of oats
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦做的，由 oat 加后缀 -en 构成

entries.definition: a small vehicle for travelling on water
entries.definitionCN: 小船，只是与 oat 拼写押韵，词源不同

entries.definition: a cereal plant grown for grain and for making beer
entries.definitionCN: 大麦，与燕麦同为性凉作物，也是酿酒谷物

entries.definition: the cereal from which flour for bread is made
entries.definitionCN: 小麦，最主要的面粉谷物

entries.definition: a hardy cereal with dark seed, used in bread
entries.definitionCN: 黑麦，耐寒的谷物，常用于做面包

entries.definition: a soft dish of cereal boiled in water or milk
entries.definitionCN: 麦片粥，燕麦粥的同类食物

normalIntro.en: Oat is a grain word that appears as a mass noun in British usage and as a plural in most other uses.
normalIntro.cn: oat 是谷物词：英国英语里常作不可数名词，其他用法多以复数 oats 出现。

normal.en: Oatmeal joins oat with meal, the word for ground grain.
normal.cn: 燕麦片一词由 oat 与表示「磨碎的谷粉」的 meal 组合而成。

normal.en: In everyday British English people say a bowl of oats for porridge.
normal.cn: 在英国英语的日常说法里，人们用「一碗 oats」指燕麦粥。

normal.en: Oat fibre and oat bran show that oat can sit before another noun as a label.
normal.cn: 燕麦纤维与燕麦麸说明 oat 可以放在另一个名词前来标示成分。

normal.en: Compare wheat and barley: these cereals use the same pattern, grain name plus food.
normal.cn: 对比 wheat 与 barley：这些谷物都遵循同样的模式——谷物名加食物名。

normal.en: Oats grow best in cool wet climates, which is why Scotland is famous for them.
normal.cn: 燕麦在凉爽湿润的气候里长得最好，这正是苏格兰燕麦有名的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a field of pale dropping seed heads swaying in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一片浅色、低垂的穗子在风中摇摆的田地。

abstract.en: Imagine the smell of warm porridge rising from a pot on a cold morning.
abstract.cn: 想象寒冷清晨，锅里升起的热燕麦粥的香气。

abstract.en: Think of a horse pushing its nose into a manger full of golden grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹马把鼻子拱进装满金黄谷粒的马槽。

examples.en: Porridge oats make a filling and cheap breakfast.
examples.cn: 燕麦片能做成管饱又便宜的早餐。

examples.en: The farmer planted oats on the wetter side of the hill.
examples.cn: 农民在山坡较湿的一侧种下了燕麦。

examples.en: Many people now choose oat milk instead of cow milk in coffee.
examples.cn: 现在很多人喝咖啡时选择燕麦奶而不是牛奶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧特」——想象早上起来吃一碗燕麦粥，时间一到就“特”别精神；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ate（燕麦）→ 中古英语 ote/oote → 英语 oat；可能受到古诺斯语同源词影响，更早的重构形式 aitan 已不可直接证实，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Oat begins as the grain and the plant grown for it, then spreads to the crop in the field, to cooked porridge, to horse feed and to a modifier before other nouns.
sensesIntro.cn: oat 先从谷粒这种作物出发，再扩展到田里的燕麦作物、煮熟的燕麦粥、喂马的饲料，以及放在其他名词前的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wind-blown field of oat with soft seed heads bowing together.
core.cn: 核心意象：风吹过成片的燕麦，柔软的穗子一起低下头。

branches.en: The grain itself is the original sense of the word.
branches.cn: 谷粒本身是这个词最原始的本义。

branches.en: The growing plants are the same grain seen in the field and counted in the plural.
branches.cn: 田间植株是同一谷粒在田里的形态，用复数计数。

branches.en: Porridge is the grain cooked and served hot.
branches.cn: 燕麦粥就是把谷粒煮熟、热着端上桌的形态。

branches.en: Feed and modifier both keep the grain but change who eats it or where it appears.
branches.cn: 饲料与定语都保留了谷粒，只改变了吃它的对象或它出现的位置。

branches.en: The wild-oat idiom turns a useless weed into a picture of youthful excess.
branches.cn: 野燕麦习语把一种无用的杂草变成了描写年轻时放纵的画面。

intro.en: Oat has no Latin prefix or suffix of its own; its word family comes from Old English, Old Norse and later English compounds such as oatmeal.
intro.cn: oat 本身不含拉丁词缀；它的词族来自古英语、古诺斯语的同源词以及后来的英语复合词，如 oatmeal。

latinIntro.en: In Latin the oats are called avena, a word still used as the scientific genus name; it is not cognate with English oat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把燕麦称作 avena，这个词今天仍是燕麦属的学名，与英语 oat 并不同源。

items.example: Old English ate is the ancestor of the modern word.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 ate 是现代 oat 的祖先。

items.meaning: the grain of a cereal plant
items.example: Oat can name the grain as a mass noun.
items.exampleCN: oat 可以作不可数名词指这种谷粒。

items.example: The plural oats names grains in the plural or a porridge.
items.exampleCN: 复数 oats 指多颗谷粒或一份燕麦粥。

items.example: Meal combines with oat in oatmeal.
items.exampleCN: meal 与 oat 组成 oatmeal。

items.example: Oatmeal is the everyday word for ground oat grain.
items.exampleCN: oatmeal 是燕麦片或燕麦粉的日常说法。

items.example: The suffix -en forms the old adjective oaten.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -en 构成旧式形容词 oaten。

items.example: Oaten describes a rough old coat in literature.
items.exampleCN: oaten 在文学作品里形容粗旧的燕麦秆织的外衣。

items.example: The suffix -y forms the casual adjective oatey.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成口语形容词 oatey。

items.example: Wild combines with oat in the phrase wild oat.
items.exampleCN: wild 与 oat 组成短语 wild oat。

items.example: Oat milk shows oat working as a modifier.
items.exampleCN: oat milk 显示 oat 作定语修饰名词。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 燕麦，与英语 oat 不同源

definition_zh: 顺从的；服从的；听话的；遵守规矩的
definition_en: willing to obey rules, orders or the wishes of someone in authority
core_image: 主人一声呼唤，趴在门口的狗立刻竖起耳朵，乖乖起身跟上去
scene: 主人在门口喊了一声，那只金毛马上叼来拖鞋，又坐回原地等着。The owner called from the doorway, and the obedient retriever brought the slippers back and sat down again.
sceneCN: 这里 obedient 是「听话的」（第 1 个义项：愿意听从他人指令）；句意：主人在门口喊了一声，那只金毛马上叼来拖鞋，又坐回原地等着。

derivatives.zh: obedient 去掉形容词后缀 -t 加名词后缀 -ence，义为「服从；顺从」
obedient 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「顺从地；听话地」
加否定前缀 dis-，义为「不服从的；违抗的」
obedient 的动词来源：拉丁语 oboedire 经法语 obeir 传入英语，义为「服从」

senses.title: Willing to follow orders
senses.definition: doing what a person in authority asks without arguing
senses.definitionCN: 不加争辩地照上级或长辈的要求去做
senses.example: The soldiers stood at attention, silent and obedient.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们立正站着，沉默而顺从。
senses.why: The Latin verb oboedire is ob plus audire, to listen to, so obedient starts as a picture of one who listens carefully to orders.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 oboedire 由 ob 与 audire（听）构成，所以 obedient 的最初形象就是「仔细听着命令的人」。

senses.title: Following the rules
senses.definition: acting according to a set of rules or a law, rather than a person
senses.definitionCN: 按照一套规则或法律行事，而不是听从某个人
senses.example: An obedient household keeps to the recycling schedule without a reminder.
senses.exampleCN: 守规矩的家庭不用提醒就会按回收时间表办事。
senses.why: Rules and laws can be obeyed just as people are, so the same adjective shifts from listeners to rule-followers.
senses.whyCN: 规则和法律可以被遵守，就像人可以听从一样，于是同一个形容词就从「听人的话」扩展到「守规则」。

senses.title: Behaving as a well-trained animal
senses.definition: of an animal, trained to follow the commands of its owner
senses.definitionCN: 指动物经过训练，能听从主人的指令
senses.example: The obedient guide dog stopped at every kerb without being told.
senses.exampleCN: 那只听话的导盲犬每到路缘都会自动停下。
senses.why: Animals that listen and respond keep the original image of listening perfectly, so the word passes from people to trained animals.
senses.whyCN: 会听指令并作出反应的动物保留了「聆听」的原始意象，于是这个词从人扩展到受过训练的动物。

senses.title: Yielding to a force or method
senses.definition: of a material, machine or method, easy to control and quick to respond
senses.definitionCN: 指材料、机器或方法容易控制、反应迅速
senses.example: People find the obedient old machine easier to use than the new one.
senses.exampleCN: 人们觉得那台听话的旧机器比新机器更好用。
senses.why: English often transfers a human quality to a thing, so an obedient machine is one that does what you ask, extending the image to objects.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把人身上的特点转移到物上，所以「听话的机器」就是按你要的去做，意象从人扩展到了工具。

senses.title: Showing the expected manner
senses.definition: in set phrases, often slightly disapproving, describing someone who never questions anything
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法里常略含贬义，形容对什么都不质疑、一味顺着的人
senses.example: Her obedient silence at the meeting worried the team leader.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上一声不吭的恭顺样子让组长有些担心。
senses.why: When obedience stops being a virtue, phrases like obedient silence turn the same word into a mild criticism.
senses.whyCN: 当「服从」不再是优点时，像「恭顺的沉默」这样的说法就把同一个词变成了轻微的批评。

intro.en: Obedient goes back to Latin oboedire, from ob, towards, and audire, to hear, so the word began as a picture of listening.
intro.cn: obedient 可上溯到拉丁语 oboedire，由 ob（朝向）与 audire（听）构成，最初的画面就是「聆听」。

items.en: The verb oboedire is built from ob plus audire, meaning to listen towards someone.
items.cn: 动词 oboedire 由 ob 加 audire 构成，字面是「朝着某人倾听」。

items.en: The present participle oboediens means listening to or obeying.
items.cn: 现在分词 oboediens 意为「倾听着、服从着的」。

items.en: The form obeissant passes into French with the same listening sense.
items.cn: 形式 obeissant 传入法语，保留同样的「聆听」义。

items.en: English takes the French participle as obedient, first describing a person under authority.
items.cn: 一般认为，英语在十三世纪借入这个法语分词，最初用来形容处于权势之下的人。

items.en: The adjective extends from people to rules, animals and machines as formal writing spreads.
items.cn: 随着正式书面语普及，形容词从人扩展到规则、动物与机器。

items.en: Obedient stays mainly formal, while obey and obedience carry the family in everyday speech.
items.cn: 现代英语里 obedient 偏正式，日常口语更多用它的家族词 obey 与 obedience。

note.en: Obedient is the listening adjective of the obey, obedience and disobedient family; its near meanings are the other words for following orders.
note.cn: obedient 是 obey、obedience、disobedient 词族中表示「听」的形容词；近义一侧则是其他表示服从的词。

entries.definition: to do what a person or rule tells you
entries.definitionCN: 服从，与 obedient 同源于拉丁语 oboedire

entries.definition: the act of obeying
entries.definitionCN: 服从；顺从，由形容词加名词后缀 -nce 构成

entries.definition: refusing to obey
entries.definitionCN: 不服从的，加否定前缀 dis- 构成

entries.definition: in an obedient way
entries.definitionCN: 顺从地，加副词后缀 -ly 构成

entries.definition: willing to agree with rules or requests
entries.definitionCN: 顺从的，偏重「按要求配合」，常用于规则与合规

entries.definition: doing what duty requires
entries.definitionCN: 尽职的、尽本分的，强调责任感而不是听从

entries.definition: too ready to accept the control of others
entries.definitionCN: 顺从的、低头的，贬义更强，强调放弃自我

entries.definition: quiet and easy to control
entries.definitionCN: 温顺的、易管教的，多形容人和动物

normalIntro.en: Obedient is literally the listening word: its Latin root audire means to hear, a root shared with audio and audible.
normalIntro.cn: obedient 字面上就是「倾听」这个词：它的拉丁词根 audire 意为「听」，audio 也出自同一个词根。

normal.en: Obedience turns the adjective into a noun, and disobedient adds dis- in front of it.
normal.cn: 名词 obedience 由形容词变形而来，disobedient 则在前面加否定前缀 dis-。

normal.en: Say obedient to someone for a person, and obedient to the rules for a rule-follower.
normal.cn: 对人说「对某人顺从」，对规则、法律说「遵守」。

normal.en: Obedient people will do as they are told, while an obedient dog sits on command.
normal.cn: 听话的人按吩咐去做，而听话的狗一喊就坐下。

normal.en: Compare audio and audible: all three share the listening root audire.
normal.cn: 对比 audio 与 audible：三者共享表示「听」的词根 audire。

normal.en: The opposite is disobedient, which is the usual word for a child who will not listen.
normal.cn: 反义词是 disobedient，常用来形容不肯听话的孩子。

abstract.en: Picture a dog whose ears prick the moment its owner calls.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗听到主人呼唤的瞬间就竖起耳朵。

abstract.en: Imagine a classroom where every hand rises at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室里，所有的手在同一瞬间举起。

abstract.en: Think of a well-trained horse turning left the moment the rein is touched.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹训练有素的马，缰绳一碰就向左转。

examples.en: The children were quiet and obedient at the museum.
examples.cn: 孩子们在博物馆里安静又听话。

examples.en: A well-trained horse is obedient to the slightest touch on its neck.
examples.cn: 训练有素的马，脖子被轻轻一碰就会听从指令。

examples.en: She nodded obediently and went back to her desk.
examples.cn: 她顺从地点了点头，回到自己的书桌前。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呃，被递走」——别人一递令，他就被带走照办，一路顺从；这纯属谐音联想，与拉丁词根 audire 无关。

root: 拉丁语 ob-（朝向）+ audire（听）→ oboedire（听从）→ 现在分词 oboediens → 古法语 obeissant → 英语 obedient，核心义是「朝着命令去听」。

sensesIntro.en: Obedient moves from a person who listens to orders, through laws and rules, to trained animals, controllable things and finally a faintly critical manner.
sensesIntro.cn: obedient 从听从命令的人出发，经过法律与规则、受训的动物、可控的事物，最后延伸到略带批评意味的言行方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dog that raises its ears and rises the moment it is called.
core.cn: 核心意象：一被呼唤就竖起耳朵、立刻起身的狗。

branches.en: Willingly following a person is the basic sense that grows straight from the listening root.
branches.cn: 愿意听从他人，是直接从「听」这一词根长出来的基本义项。

branches.en: Following rules instead of people is the same habit aimed at a code.
branches.cn: 从听人转向守规则，是同一种习惯指向一套准则。

branches.en: Trained animals are the listening image applied to creatures that obey commands.
branches.cn: 受训的动物，就是「聆听」意象落在听从指令的生物身上。

branches.en: An obedient machine is the human quality lent to an object.
branches.cn: 听话的机器，是把人的特质借用到了物上。

branches.en: Excessive obedience shades into the mildly critical manner set phrases describe.
branches.cn: 过分的服从会滑向固定说法中那种略带批评的言行方式。

intro.en: Obedient is built from a Latin verb and an English adjective ending; its wider family includes obediently, obedience and disobedient.
intro.cn: obedient 由拉丁语动词与英语形容词后缀构成；它更广的词族包括 obediently、obedience 与 disobedient。

latinIntro.en: Latin oboedire means to listen to and to obey, while audire means to hear; the two Latin pieces are the core of this word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oboedire 意为「听从」，audire 意为「听」；这两个拉丁成分构成了这个词的核心。

items.example: The prefix ob- points the listening towards the speaker.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ob- 把「听」这个动作指向说话的人。

items.example: Audire is the hearing root shared with audio and audible.
items.exampleCN: audire 是与 audio、audible 共享的「听」词根。

items.example: Oboedire fuses listening with doing what is asked.
items.exampleCN: oboedire 把「听」与「照办」合成一个动作。

items.meaningCN: 表示「正在……的」形容词词尾
items.example: The ending -ent makes a participle into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 把分词变成形容词。

items.example: Obedient describes a person or animal under authority.
items.exampleCN: obedient 形容处于权势之下的人或动物。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb obediently.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 obediently。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The noun ending gives obedience.
items.exampleCN: 名词词尾构成 obedience。

items.example: The prefix dis- reverses the adjective in disobedient.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 dis- 在 disobedient 中把形容词的意思反转。

items.example: Obey is the shortened verb of the same Latin source.
items.exampleCN: obey 是同一拉丁来源的动词缩略形式。

definition_zh: 使物化；把……当作物品看待；使具体化；客观表达
definition_en: to treat a person as a thing rather than a human being, or to make something abstract into a concrete thing
core_image: 一个活生生的人被贴上一张标签，变成货架上的一件商品
scene: 广告把模特当作纯粹的推销工具，只看身材不看人。The advertisement objectifies the model, treating her as a product rather than a person.
sceneCN: 这里 objectify 是「物化」（第 1 个义项：把人当作物品看待）；句意：这则广告物化了模特，把她当作商品而不是人。

pos.zh: 使物化；把……当作物品看待

collocations.zh: 被性化的；被当作性对象的

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ification 后缀构成，义为「物化；对象化」
由现在分词形容词化，义为「物化的；使人沦为物体的」
基础词，义为「物体；对象」以及「反对」（作动词时重音后移）
由 object 加 -ive 构成，义为「客观的」与「目标」

senses.title: To treat a person as a thing
senses.definition: to treat someone as an object without human feelings or dignity, often in sexual or commercial contexts
senses.definitionCN: 无视人的情感与尊严，把某人当作物品看待，常见于性或商业语境
senses.example: Some adverts objectify women by reducing them to their bodies.
senses.exampleCN: 一些广告把女性简化为身体，从而物化了她们。
senses.why: Object comes from Latin obiectum, something thrown in the way, and the English suffix -ify turns a noun into a verb, so objectify literally makes a being into a mere thing.
senses.whyCN: object 源自拉丁语 obiectum（抛在面前的东西），英语后缀 -ify 使名词变为动词，所以 objectify 字面意思就是「把存在变成纯粹的物」。

senses.title: To make something abstract concrete
senses.definition: to express or represent an abstract idea in a visible or tangible form
senses.definitionCN: 把抽象观念表达或呈现为看得见、摸得着的形式
senses.example: The architect tried to objectify the idea of light in a solid wall.
senses.exampleCN: 这位建筑师试图用一面实墙把光的理念具体化。
senses.why: The same suffix also means to make an object out of something intangible, so a thought can be given solid form.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也可以指「把无形之物做成实物」，因此一个想法可以被赋予实体形态。

senses.title: To describe something objectively
senses.definition: to present feelings, opinions, or emotions in a detached and neutral way
senses.definitionCN: 以超然而中立的笔调呈现感受、看法或情绪
senses.example: The poet objectifies her grief by describing a bare winter field.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人用一片荒凉的冬野来客观化自己的悲伤。
senses.why: Moving a feeling into the outside world makes it an object that can be looked at rather than felt only from inside.
senses.whyCN: 把情感搬到外部世界，它就成了一件可以被观看的对象，而不只是内心里的感受。

senses.title: A posture of detached professionalism
senses.titleCN: 把对象规整化的职业姿态
senses.definition: the habit of turning people, work, or nature into measurable items to be handled and counted
senses.definitionCN: 把人、工作或自然转成可衡量条目以便处理和计数的习惯
senses.example: The report was praised for how it objectifies the data without losing the story.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告因把数据对象化却又不失故事性而受到称赞。
senses.why: Once something can be handled, measured, and counted, an institution can manage it without engaging with its inner life.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物可以被处理、衡量、计数，机构就可以管理它，而不必关心它的内在世界。

intro.en: Objectify is formed inside English from object plus the French-Latin suffix -ify, so its history is the history of object.
intro.cn: objectify 是在英语内部由 object 加上法拉丁语来源的后缀 -ify 构成的，因此它的历史就是 object 的历史。

items.en: Obiectum is a thing thrown before the mind, from ob, against, and iacere, to throw.
items.cn: obiectum 指被投放到心灵前方之物，来自 ob（对着）与 iacere（投掷）。

items.en: Late scholars use obiectum for what is opposed to a subject in thought.
items.cn: 晚期学者用 obiectum 表示思考中与主体相对立的一方。

items.en: The form object passes into French and then into Middle English.
items.cn: object 这一形式先进入法语，再传入中古英语。

items.en: The suffix -ify, from Latin -ificare, attaches to nouns to make verbs of turning.
items.cn: 后缀 -ify 来自拉丁语 -ificare，附在名词后构成表示「变成」的动词。

items.en: Philosophical writers use objectify for giving outward form to inner thoughts.
items.cn: 哲学家们用 objectify 表示给内心思想以外部形式。

items.en: Twentieth century critics extend it to treating people as things in society.
items.cn: 二十世纪的批评家把它扩展为在社会中把人当作物对待。

note.en: Objectify is one direction of the object family, pointing at turning a being into a thing, close to reify, dehumanise, and commodify.
note.cn: objectify 是 object 词族中的一端，指向「把存在变成物」，与 reify、dehumanise、commodify 相邻。

entries.definition: a material thing that can be seen and touched
entries.definitionCN: 可以看见和触摸的实物

entries.definition: not influenced by personal feelings
entries.definitionCN: 不受个人感情影响的；客观的

entries.definition: a statement of disagreement
entries.definitionCN: 反对意见

entries.definition: the act of treating a person as a thing
entries.definitionCN: 物化；对象化的行为

entries.definition: to treat an abstract idea as if it were a real thing
entries.definitionCN: 把抽象概念当作真实事物对待

entries.definition: to turn something into a product to be bought and sold
entries.definitionCN: 把某物商品化

entries.definition: to take away the human qualities of a person
entries.definitionCN: 使失去人性；使人非人化

normalIntro.en: Objectify is object plus the verb-making suffix -ify, so it shows the moment a thing or a thought is turned into an object.
normalIntro.cn: objectify 是 object 加上构成动词的后缀 -ify，呈现的是「物」或「想法」被变成对象的那个瞬间。

normal.en: Object plus -ify equals objectify, making someone or something into an object.
normal.cn: object 加 -ify 就是 objectify，即把人或物变成对象。

normal.en: The noun objectification keeps the same core and names the act.
normal.cn: 名词 objectification 保留同一核心，指这种行为的本身。

normal.en: Related words in the -ify pattern include clarify, purify, and reify.
normal.cn: 同样用 -ify 的还有「clarify」「purify」与「reify」。

normal.en: Compare the adjective objective, which shares the root but means fair and neutral.
normal.cn: 对比形容词 objective：同根，但意思是客观公正的。

normal.en: In sexist media discussion objectify is the standard verb for treating women as bodies.
normal.cn: 在性别议题的讨论中，objectify 是「把女性当作身体」的固定动词。

abstract.en: Imagine a portrait path where a face slowly fades into a mannequin.
abstract.cn: 想象一张人像正在慢慢褪色，最后变成商店橱窗里的假人模特。

abstract.en: See a fog of worry being poured into a glass jar and sealed tight.
abstract.cn: 想象一团担忧的雾气被倒进玻璃罐里，然后被牢牢封住。

abstract.en: Picture a poet holding her tears at arm length and drawing them as a frozen lake.
abstract.cn: 想象一位诗人把手伸直，远远端着眼泪，把它画成一汪结冰的湖。

examples.en: Critics argue that reality shows objectify the people who take part in them.
examples.cn: 评论家认为，真人秀把参与其中的人物化了。

examples.en: The museum tried to objectify memory through two hundred ordinary letters.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆试图用两百封普通信件把记忆具体化。

examples.en: She objectified her pain in a single sentence about an empty chair.
examples.cn: 她用一句关于空椅子的话把痛苦客观化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，不，解体的」——把活生生的人看成可以拆解的零件，就是物化；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 obiectum（抛在面前之物，来自 ob 对着 + iacere 投掷）→ object（物体）＋拉丁语 -ificare 来源的 -ify（使……化）→ objectify，核心义「把一个存在降格为物」。

sensesIntro.en: Objectify starts from the blunt image of turning a person into a thing, then widens to making an idea concrete, describing feelings objectively, and finally the routine habit of handling people and data as countable items.
sensesIntro.cn: objectify 起于「把人变成物」的直白意象，再扩展到把想法具体化、客观地表达感受，最后指把人或数据当作可计数的条目来处理的习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a living face turning into a label on a shop shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张活生生的脸变成货架上的标签。

branches.en: Treating a person as a thing is the sharpest and most used sense.
branches.cn: 把人当作物是最锋利、最常用的义项。

branches.en: Giving an idea solid form is the constructive sense.
branches.cn: 给想法以实体形态是建设性的义项。

branches.en: Expressing feeling objectively grows from the same making an object of what is inside.
branches.cn: 客观地表达感受同样源自「把内心之物做成对象」。

branches.en: Both senses share the habit of seeing living things as items to be counted.
branches.cn: 这两个义项共享同一种习惯：把有生命的东西看成可以计数的条目。

branches.en: Art and philosophy use both to move inward states into visible outer form.
branches.cn: 艺术与哲学都用这两义把内在状态搬到可见的外部形式中。

intro.en: Objectify is a noun turned verb: object plus -ify, with the whole object family and the -ification noun around it.
intro.cn: objectify 是名词转动词：object 加 -ify，周围是整个 object 词族以及 -ification 构成的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin obiectum means that which is thrown before, and iacere means to throw.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 obiectum 意为「被抛在面前之物」，iacere 意为投掷。

items.example: The prefix ob- gives the sense of being placed in front.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ob- 表示「被放在前面」。

items.example: Iacere also gives the verb project.
items.exampleCN: iacere 还构成动词「project」。

items.example: Obiectum is the direct source of object.
items.exampleCN: obiectum 是 object 的直接来源。

items.meaning: a thing you can see and touch
items.example: Object is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: object 是整个词族的基础。

items.meaning: to make or cause to be
items.example: The suffix -ify turns the noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 把名词变成动词。

items.example: Objectify names the act of turning into a thing.
items.exampleCN: objectify 指把事物变成物体这一行为。

items.meaning: the act or process of making
items.example: The suffix -ification forms objectification.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ification 构成 objectification。

items.meaning: the act of treating as an object
items.example: Objectification keeps the abstract name of the act.
items.exampleCN: objectification 是这一行为的名词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms the adjective objective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成形容词 objective。

definition_zh: 斜的；倾斜的；间接的；拐弯抹角的；斜角的
definition_en: slanted rather than straight, or expressed indirectly rather than openly
core_image: 一面墙没有正对着你，而是斜斜地切过来
scene: 画家在画面里留出一条斜线，让视线被悄悄带向远处的船。The painter placed an oblique line across the canvas to pull the eye toward the distant boat.
sceneCN: 这里 oblique 是「斜的」（第 1 个义项：与直线或直角成斜角）；句意：画家在画布上画了一条斜线，把目光引向远处的小船。

pos.zh: 间接的；拐弯抹角的；含蓄的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「斜着；间接地」
由拉丁语 obliquitas 借入，义为「倾斜；不直率」
形容词加 -ness，义为「倾斜程度；不直率」

senses.title: Slanted at an angle
senses.definition: neither vertical nor horizontal, but set at an angle to a straight line
senses.definitionCN: 既不竖直也不水平，而是与直线成一定斜角
senses.example: The sun cast oblique shadows across the courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光在院子里投下斜斜的影子。
senses.why: Latin obliquus describes something turned sideway, so the core picture is a line that refuses to stand straight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obliquus 描述的是转向一侧的东西，所以核心画面是一条不肯站直的线。

senses.title: Indirect in meaning
senses.definition: said or done in a roundabout way, not stated directly or openly
senses.definitionCN: 以绕弯子的方式说出或做出，并不直接公开表达
senses.example: He made an oblique remark about the manager poor timekeeping habits.
senses.exampleCN: 他含沙射影地提到经理不守时的毛病。
senses.why: A line that does not go straight can also describe speech that does not go straight to the point.
senses.whyCN: 不走的直线同样可以形容不直说的言辞，所以「斜」自然引申为「绕」。

senses.title: An angled line or face
senses.definition: a sloping line, surface, or plane seen in drawing, geometry, or architecture
senses.definitionCN: 在绘图、几何或建筑中出现的斜线、斜面或斜切面
senses.example: The light comes in through an oblique plane of glass.
senses.exampleCN: 光线从一块斜面的玻璃中透进来。
senses.why: The adjective also names the thing itself, so an oblique is a visible slanted surface in space.
senses.whyCN: 形容词同时也可以指称事物本身，因此 an oblique 就是空间里看得见的斜面。

senses.title: The grammatical oblique case
senses.definition: a case form of a noun used for anything other than the subject, such as object or possession
senses.definitionCN: 名词用于主语以外用途（如宾语、领属）的格形式
senses.example: Latin changed the noun into the oblique case after a preposition.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语在介词后把名词变成间接格。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the image of a line that is not the main straight one, so any non subject form became an oblique.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借用了「不走主干直线」的意象，于是所有非主语形式都被称为间接格。

intro.en: Oblique comes from Latin obliquus, slanted or sideward, probably from the twister ob, across, and licinus, bent.
intro.cn: oblique 来自拉丁语 obliquus（斜的、向一侧的），一般认为由 ob（横过）与 licinus（弯曲的）组合而来。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to bend or to turn may lie behind licinus.
items.cn: licinus 背后可能有一个重构的、表示「弯曲、转向」的词根，存疑。

items.en: Obliquus is used of lines, eyes, and looks that are not straight ahead.
items.cn: 拉丁语 obliquus 用于形容不朝向正前方的线、目光与视线。

items.en: Grammarians call cases other than the nominative cases obliqui.
items.cn: 语法家把主格以外的格称为 cases obliqui。

items.en: The word becomes oblique in French with the same slanted meaning.
items.cn: 该词在法语中写作 oblique，保留「斜」的含义。

items.en: English borrows oblique for geometry, grammar, and indirect speech.
items.cn: 英语借入 oblique，用于几何、语法与间接表达。

items.en: Later usage adds oblique criticism and oblique reference in social discourse.
items.cn: 后来用法又在社交语境中加入「拐弯抹角的批评」与「暗指」。

note.en: Oblique looks close to obliquity and obliquely, and its meaning area overlaps with slanted, indirect, and evasive words.
note.cn: oblique 与 obliquity、obliquely 形近同根，其义域与表示倾斜、间接、闪避的词重叠。

entries.definition: at an angle, or indirectly
entries.definitionCN: 斜着地；间接地

entries.definition: the state of being slanted or not straightforward
entries.definitionCN: 倾斜状态；不直率

entries.definition: to make someone do something by rule or duty
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写开头相近，词源不同，意为「迫使；施恩」

entries.definition: set at a sloping angle
entries.definitionCN: 倾斜的；斜向的

entries.definition: not going straight to the point
entries.definitionCN: 间接的

entries.definition: deliberately unclear or avoiding a direct answer
entries.definitionCN: 回避的；含糊其词的

normalIntro.en: Oblique is the Latin word for what goes sideways rather than straight, and the same picture explains its indirect sense.
normalIntro.cn: oblique 是拉丁语中表示「走向一侧而非笔直」的词，同一画面也解释了它「间接」的意思。

normal.en: An oblique angle is neither a right angle nor a straight line.
normal.cn: 斜角既不是直角也不是直线。

normal.en: The adverb obliquely means in a slanted or roundabout way.
normal.cn: 副词 obliquely 表示斜着或绕着弯子。

normal.en: The noun obliquity names the quality of being oblique.
normal.cn: 名词 obliquity 表示「倾斜」这一性质。

normal.en: Grammar keeps the phrase the oblique case for non subject forms.
normal.cn: 语法中保留「间接格」这一说法，用来指非主语形式。

normal.en: Common collocations include oblique reference, oblique criticism, and oblique line.
normal.cn: 常见搭配有「oblique reference」「oblique criticism」与「oblique line」。

abstract.en: Imagine a ladder leaning against a wall instead of standing upright.
abstract.cn: 想象一把梯子没有立直，而是斜靠在墙上。

abstract.en: Picture a guest hinting at a complaint instead of saying it aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一位客人不明说不满，只是绕着弯子提示。

abstract.en: See a slice of glass cut across a cube at a sharp slant.
abstract.cn: 想象一块立方体被斜斜地切下一片玻璃。

examples.en: The path leaves the main road at an oblique angle.
examples.cn: 这条小路以一个斜角从大路上岔开。

examples.en: His oblique comments suggested that the plan would fail.
examples.cn: 他那些拐弯抹角的话暗示计划会失败。

examples.en: The book makes several oblique references to the war.
examples.cn: 这本书几处间接地提到了那场战争。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「握不直」——手里握着一根杆子怎么也扶不直，总是歪着，就是斜的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ob（横过、对着一侧）+ licinus（弯曲的）→ obliquus（斜的）→ 古法语 oblique → 英语 oblique，核心义「不笔直，转向一侧」。

sensesIntro.en: Oblique moves from the physical picture of a slanted line to the indirect style of speech, to the sloping surface itself, and finally to the grammar label for non subject cases.
sensesIntro.cn: oblique 从「斜线」的物理画面走到言辞的间接方式，再指斜面本身，最后成为语法中非主语格的名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall cutting across your path at a slant.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面墙斜斜地横切过你眼前的路。

branches.en: The literal slanted line is the base sense.
branches.cn: 字面的斜线是基础义项。

branches.en: Indirect speech follows the same refusal to go straight.
branches.cn: 间接之言沿用了「不直走」的同一逻辑。

branches.en: A sloping surface is the physical object seen at a slant.
branches.cn: 斜面是被斜着看到的那件实物。

branches.en: Grammar names any non subject case an oblique.
branches.cn: 语法把一切非主语格都称为间接格。

branches.en: Both describe geometry where lines meet at an angle other than a right angle.
branches.cn: 两者都描述线与线以非直角相交的几何情形。

intro.en: Oblique has no strong English affix structure; it entered as a whole Latin adjective and grew adverbs and nouns from there.
intro.cn: oblique 没有明显的英语词缀结构，它是作为一个完整的拉丁语形容词进入英语的，随后才派生出副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ob means across or in front of, and licinus means bent or crooked.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ob 表示「横过、在前方」，licinus 表示「弯曲的、歪的」。

items.example: The prefix ob- adds the idea of crossing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ob- 带来「横穿」的意味。

items.example: Licinus supplies the bent image.
items.exampleCN: licinus 提供「弯曲」的意象。

items.example: Obliquus is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: obliquus 是直接来源。

items.example: Oblique keeps both senses in English.
items.exampleCN: oblique 在英语中保留了两个义项。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms obliquely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 obliquely。

items.example: Obliquely marks how the action is done.
items.exampleCN: obliquely 说明动作的方式。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms obliquity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 obliquity。

items.example: Obliquity names the quality.
items.exampleCN: obliquity 指这种性质。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms obliqueness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 obliqueness。

definition_zh: 双簧管；英国管；吹双簧管的人
definition_en: a woodwind instrument with a thin double reed, a pale slim body, and a clear slightly nasal tone
core_image: 一支细细的木管插着两片薄簧，簧片一颤便发出尖而清亮的音
scene: 乐团调音时，双簧管先奏出一个长音，其他乐器再跟着对准。At the start of the concert, the oboe played a long note so the rest of the orchestra could tune to it.
sceneCN: 这里 oboe 是「双簧管」（第 1 个义项：一种吹奏的双簧木管乐器）；句意：音乐会开场时，双簧管吹出一个长音，让整个乐团照着调音。

pos.zh: 双簧管类乐器；相关的管乐声部
吹双簧管的人；双簧管手

derivatives.zh: 由 oboe 加 -ist 构成，义为「吹双簧管的人」
由 oboe 与 family 组成的复合名称，义为「双簧管一族」
由 oboe 与意大利语 amore 构成的复合名称，义为「柔音双簧管」
oboe 的早期英语拼写形式

senses.title: A double reed woodwind instrument
senses.definition: a slender wooden wind instrument with two thin reeds that vibrate against each other to make a bright reedy sound
senses.definitionCN: 一种细长的木质管乐器，靠两片薄簧相互振动发出明亮、带簧片味的音色
senses.example: The oboe opened the movement with a long quiet phrase.
senses.exampleCN: 双簧管用一句悠长安静的音打开了这一乐章。
senses.why: The name comes from French hautbois, high wood, because the early instrument had a bright high voice compared with the older shawm.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自法语 hautbois（高亢的木头），因为早期的乐器比更早的哨管（竖笛）声音更高更亮。

senses.title: The oboe family and its parts
senses.definition: the group of related double reed instruments, such as the English horn and the bass oboe, and the reeds and mouthpieces used with them
senses.definitionCN: 一组相关的双簧木管乐器，如英国管与低音双簧管，以及与之配套的簧片和吹口
senses.example: The ensemble used the oboe family to cover the middle voices.
senses.exampleCN: 这个合奏团体用双簧管族来承担中声部。
senses.why: Once oboe became the family name, its relatives and parts were all called oboe with a modifier in front.
senses.whyCN: oboe 一旦成为族名，它的亲属与配件就都用 oboe 加限定词来称呼。

senses.title: A player of the oboe
senses.definition: a person who plays the oboe, usually called an oboist
senses.definitionCN: 吹双簧管的人，正式说法是 oboist
senses.example: The new oboe joined the orchestra straight from college.
senses.exampleCN: 那位新来的双簧管手刚从学院毕业就加入了乐团。
senses.why: English often lets an instrument name stand for its player, and oboe was used this way before oboist became the standard form.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用乐器名代指演奏者，在 oboist 成为标准说法之前，oboe 就是这样被使用的。

senses.title: A familiar reedy tone
senses.definition: the thin, clear, slightly nasal tone associated with the instrument, often used as an image for something plaintive
senses.definitionCN: 与这种乐器相联的细、清、略带鼻音的音色，常被用作哀怨之物的意象
senses.example: Her voice had an oboe quality that carried across the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音带有一种双簧管般的音色，传遍了整个大厅。
senses.why: A sound that is easy to recognise also becomes a mental picture for other sounds that share its shape.
senses.whyCN: 一种容易被认出的声音，也会成为其他相似声音的心理画面。

intro.en: Oboe is a French word wearing Italian clothes: hautbois, high wood, was shortened and spelled the Italian way.
intro.cn: oboe 是一个穿了意大利外衣的法语词：hautbois（高亢的木管）缩短后，被按意大利语的方式拼写。

items.en: Haut means high and bois means wood, so hautbois is the high wood.
items.cn: haut 意为「高的」，bois 意为「木头」，所以 hautbois 就是「高亢的木管」。

items.en: Hautbois names a band of loud reed players and their instruments.
items.cn: hautbois 指一队响亮的簧管乐手以及他们所用乐器。

items.en: Paris makers develop a refined two reed instrument that keeps the name hautbois.
items.cn: 巴黎的制琴师改良出精致的双簧乐器，仍沿用 hautbois 这个名字。

items.en: Italian musicians write the borrowed word as oboe, matching their spelling habits.
items.cn: 意大利乐师把这个借词写作 oboe，符合他们的拼写习惯。

items.en: The Italian form oboe enters English and replaces the older spelling hautboy.
items.cn: 意大利语形式 oboe 进入英语，取代了较早的 hauboy 拼法。

items.en: Oboe now names the instrument, its family, and its standing role for tuning.
items.cn: 现代英语中 oboe 指这种乐器、它的族类，以及它调音的固定角色。

note.en: Oboe is close in spelling to oboist and oboe d amore, and it sits among other woodwind and double reed words.
note.cn: oboe 与 oboist、oboe d amore 拼写形近，并与其它木管与双簧类词汇相邻。

entries.definition: a person who plays the oboe
entries.definitionCN: 吹双簧管的人

entries.definition: the French name from which oboe comes
entries.definitionCN: oboe 所由来的法语原名

entries.definition: a softer voiced oboe pitched a minor third lower
entries.definitionCN: 音色更柔、比双簧管低小三度的乐器

entries.definition: a low pitched double reed woodwind instrument
entries.definitionCN: 低音双簧木管乐器

entries.definition: a woodwind instrument played with a single reed
entries.definitionCN: 单簧木管乐器

entries.definition: the English horn, a larger oboe with a mellow tone
entries.definitionCN: 英国管，一种音色柔和的较大双簧管

normalIntro.en: Oboe is a short word hiding a French phrase, and the picture of a high thin wooden pipe makes it stick.
normalIntro.cn: oboe 这个短词里藏着一个法语短语，再配上「又高又细的木管」的画面就很容易记住。

normal.en: Oboe comes from French hautbois, where haut means high and bois means wood.
normal.cn: oboe 来自法语 hautbois，其中 haut 是「高」，bois 是「木头」。

normal.en: The player is an oboist, formed by adding -ist to oboe.
normal.cn: 演奏者叫 oboist，由 oboe 加 -ist 构成。

normal.en: Older English texts write the instrument as hautboy before oboe wins.
normal.cn: 较早的英语文本把这种乐器写作 hautboy，后来 oboe 才胜出。

normal.en: Band and orchestra members tune to the oboe because its pitch stays steady.
normal.cn: 乐队和乐团都以双簧管调音，因为它的音高比较稳定。

normal.en: Related woodwind words include clarinet, bassoon, and flute.
normal.cn: 相关的木管乐器词还有「clarinet」「bassoon」与「flute」。

abstract.en: Picture a slim wooden pipe with two thin lips at the top breathing a clear cry.
abstract.cn: 想象一支细木管，顶端两片薄薄的「嘴唇」一颤，发出一声清亮的叫喊。

abstract.en: See an orchestra going quiet as one pale wooden voice marks the tuning note.
abstract.cn: 想象整个乐团安静下来，只听一个发白的木质嗓音定出调音的那个音。

abstract.en: Imagine a person sitting in the back row but known by name for the instrument.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人坐在后排，却因手上的乐器而被人指名道姓地记住。

examples.en: She has played the oboe since she was nine years old.
examples.cn: 她从九岁起就开始吹双簧管。

examples.en: The oboe solo brought a cold, clear colour to the winter scene.
examples.cn: 双簧管独奏为冬天场景带来一种清冷明亮的色彩。

examples.en: Two oboes and a bassoon formed the small woodwind group.
examples.cn: 两支双簧管和一支巴松组成这个小木管组。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦啵」——两片簧片一碰就发出「啵」的一声，接着吹出长长的「哦」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 haut（高的）＋ bois（木头）→ hautbois（高亢的木管）→ 意大利语拼写 oboe → 英语 oboe，核心义「声音高而亮的细木管」。

sensesIntro.en: Oboe starts as the name of one slender reed instrument, then stretches to its family and parts, to the player, and finally to a recognisable tone colour.
sensesIntro.cn: oboe 起初只是一种细长簧管乐器的名字，接着扩展到它的族类与构件、演奏者，最后成为一种可辨认的音色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin wooden pipe cut through by two trembling reeds.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支细木管顶端由两片颤动的簧片吹响。

branches.en: The single instrument is the base sense.
branches.cn: 单一的乐器是基础义项。

branches.en: The family and parts extend the base name with modifiers.
branches.cn: 族类与构件是在本名上加限定词扩展出来的。

branches.en: The player is named by the instrument itself.
branches.cn: 演奏者用乐器本身的名字来指称。

branches.en: The tone colour carries the instrument into metaphor.
branches.cn: 音色把这种乐器带进了比喻。

branches.en: Both point at the same double reed construction shared by English horn and bass oboe.
branches.cn: 两者都指向英国管与低音双簧管共有的同一种双簧构造。

intro.en: Oboe is a whole borrowed word rather than a built form, yet its short stem supports oboist and the compound family names.
intro.cn: oboe 是整体借入的词，而不是拼装出来的形式，但它的短词干仍然支撑着 oboist 以及各复合族名。

latinIntro.en: Oboe has no Latin ancestry; it descends from French hautbois, a compound of a Germanic high and a Late Latin wood word.
latinIntro.cn: oboe 没有拉丁语祖先，它来自法语 hautbois，由日耳曼来源的「高」和晚期拉丁语的「木头」复合而成。

items.example: Haut is the Germanic element meaning high.
items.exampleCN: haut 是源自日耳曼语的「高」这一成分。

items.example: Bois traces through Late Latin boscus to Germanic bush.
items.exampleCN: bois 经由晚期拉丁语 boscus 追溯到日耳曼语的「灌木」。

items.example: Hautbois is the source of oboe.
items.exampleCN: hautbois 是 oboe 的来源。

items.example: Oboe is the settled English form.
items.exampleCN: oboe 是最终定型的英语形式。

items.example: Hautboy was once the common spelling.
items.exampleCN: hautboy 曾是常见拼法。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms oboist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 oboist。

items.example: Oboist names the person rather than the object.
items.exampleCN: oboist 指人而不指物。

items.meaning: the group of double reed instruments
items.example: The oboe family covers several sizes and registers.
items.exampleCN: 双簧管族包含多个尺寸与音域。

items.example: Oboe d amore appears in baroque scores.
items.exampleCN: 柔音双簧管常见于巴洛克乐谱。

definition_zh: 淫秽的；猥亵的；伤风败俗的；令人反感的；过分的
definition_en: dealing with sex in a way that is offensive or shocks most people, or so extreme that it seems shocking
core_image: 一块污物落在白布上，旁人的脸色立刻变了
scene: 地铁车厢里有人外放一段污言秽语的视频，周围乘客纷纷皱眉。A passenger played an obscene video on the subway, and the people nearby turned away.
sceneCN: 这里 obscene 是「淫秽的」（第 1 个义项：露骨涉性、令人反感的）；句意：一名乘客在地铁上播放一段淫秽视频，附近的人都转过头去。

pos.zh: 淫秽的；猥亵的；伤风败俗的
令人反感的；为逞私欲而不顾廉耻的

derivatives.zh: 由 obscene 加 -ity 构成，义为「淫秽；淫秽的语言或图像」
由 obscene 加 -ly 构成，义为「下流地；过分地」
由 obscene 加 -ness 构成，义为「淫秽性；下流」，书面语，较少见

senses.title: Offensive to decency
senses.definition: showing or describing sex in a way that shocks ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 以令常人震惊的方式表现或描写性场面的
senses.example: The shop window displayed an obscene poster.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店的橱窗里摆着一张淫秽海报。
senses.why: Latin ob means against and scenum means what is off the stage, so the word first named what decent people must not see.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ob 表示「违背」，scenum 指「不上台的东西」，所以这个词最初就指正派人不能看的东西。

senses.title: Doing wrong without shame
senses.titleCN: 伤风败俗的；明目张胆作恶的
senses.definition: shamelessly wicked or done openly without any sense of shame
senses.definitionCN: 厚颜无耻地作恶，或毫无羞耻地公开行事
senses.example: He made an obscene amount of money from the fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠这场骗局赚了一大笔黑心钱。
senses.why: The old sources also use the word for anything shamelessly foul, so it slides from sexual indecency to any open wrong.
senses.whyCN: 早期文献里这个词也指任何厚颜无耻的丑恶之事，于是由性方面的不雅滑向一切公然的恶行。

senses.title: Shockingly excessive
senses.definition: so large or extreme that it shocks or offends people
senses.definitionCN: 大得或极端得令人震惊、令人不适的
senses.example: The corner shop charges obscene prices for bottled water.
senses.exampleCN: 那家街角小店的瓶装水卖得贵得离谱。
senses.why: Once the word means what offends good taste, it can also brand a sum or a lifestyle as indecently large.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「冒犯体面」，它也能把一个数目或一种生活方式标为「大得不像话」。

intro.en: Scholars generally trace obscene to Latin obscenus, the spelling of which was later altered under the influence of caenum, mud.
intro.cn: 一般认为 obscene 来自拉丁语 obscenus，其拼写后来受 caenum（污泥）影响而变成现在的样子。

items.en: Obscenus marks bad omens, filth, and words that bring ill luck.
items.cn: obscenus 指凶兆、污秽以及招来厄运的话。

items.en: Roman writers use the word for indecency and for what shames the eyes.
items.cn: 罗马作家用它指不雅之事和不该让人看见的东西。

items.en: Grammarians link the word with caenum, mud, which fixes the meaning as filth.
items.cn: 语法学家把它同 caenum（污泥）联系起来，使「污秽」这一含义固定下来。

items.en: Obscene enters French as a bookish word for lewd and filthy.
items.cn: obscene 进入法语，作为书面词表示淫秽、肮脏。

items.en: English adopts obscene, first for indecency and omens, then for sexual indecency.
items.cn: 英语借入 obscene，先指不雅与凶兆，后来专指性的不雅。

items.en: The word becomes the legal term for indecency and moves into phrases for shocking excess.
items.cn: 这个词成为法律上指「淫秽」的术语，并衍生出表示「过分」的短语。

note.en: Obscene belongs to the Latin word for bad omen and filth, and it stands next to indecent, lewd, and vulgar.
note.cn: obscene 源于拉丁语表示凶兆与污秽的词，在词形上与 obscenity、obscenely 相邻，在意义上与 indecent、lewd、vulgar 相邻。

entries.definition: something offensive and indecent
entries.definitionCN: 由 obscene 加 -ity 构成的名词，指淫秽的事物

entries.definition: in an indecent or shockingly extreme way
entries.definitionCN: 由 obscene 加 -ly 构成的副词，指下流地或过分地

entries.definition: not well known or hard to see
entries.definitionCN: 晦暗的；难懂的，只是与 obscene 拼写相近，词源不同：obscure 来自表示「遮盖」的拉丁词

entries.definition: offending accepted standards of behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 不得体的；有伤风化的，比 obscene 语气温和

entries.definition: showing an offensive interest in sex
entries.definitionCN: 淫荡的；猥亵的，多用在法律语境，书面色彩较强

entries.definition: rude or lacking good taste
entries.definitionCN: 粗俗的；庸俗的，侧重粗野无礼而非色情

normalIntro.en: Obscene is the adjective of filth and bad omen, and the law and the press both use it.
normalIntro.cn: obscene 是表示「污秽」与「凶兆」的形容词，法律与新闻都在用。

normal.en: The law bans obscene publications but allows artistic ones.
normal.cn: 法律禁止淫秽出版物，但允许有艺术价值的作品。

normal.en: The child was shown obscene gestures by an older boy.
normal.cn: 一个较大的男孩对孩子做了下流手势。

normal.en: Obscene language is a phrase for swearing that shocks.
normal.cn: obscene language 是表达「粗话、污言秽语」的固定说法。

normal.en: In stories about money, obscene often means shockingly large.
normal.cn: 在谈钱的语境里，obscene 常表示「大得惊人」。

normal.en: Compare indecent: indecent is milder and covers manners, obscene is stronger and usually sexual.
normal.cn: 对比 indecent：indecent 语气温和且涉及举止，obscene 更强烈，多指涉性内容。

abstract.en: Picture a dirty spot on clean linen that makes the viewer look away.
abstract.cn: 想象干净床单上的一处污点，让看的人马上移开视线。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker who curses in public without any shame.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在公共场合毫无羞耻地满口脏话。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag with a number so big it looks indecent.
abstract.cn: 想象价签上的数字大得让人难以接受。

examples.en: The court heard that the programme contained obscene material.
examples.cn: 法庭获悉该节目含有淫秽内容。

examples.en: It is illegal to sell obscene images to children.
examples.cn: 向儿童出售淫秽图片是违法的。

examples.en: Some bankers earned obscene bonuses while the firm lost money.
examples.cn: 公司亏钱时，有些银行家仍拿到了高得离谱的奖金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恶不嫌」——恶俗的东西居然「不嫌」羞，就叫人觉得淫秽、下流；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 obscenus（凶兆、污秽、不祥之语）→ 拼写受 caenum（污泥）影响变为 obscenus → 法语 obscene → 英语 obscene，核心义「冒犯体面、污秽不堪」。

sensesIntro.en: Obscene starts as a word for filth and bad omen, becomes the legal tag for sexual indecency, then spreads to shameless wrongs and shockingly large amounts.
sensesIntro.cn: obscene 从表示污秽与凶兆的词开始，成为指性的不雅的法律标签，再扩展到厚颜无耻的恶行和令人震惊的巨大数量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stain that makes people look away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一处让人不忍直视的污迹。

branches.en: Sexual indecency is the dominant sense today.
branches.cn: 涉性的不雅是今天最主要的意思。

branches.en: Shameless open wrong comes from the older filth sense.
branches.cn: 厚颜无耻的公然作恶来自更早的污秽义。

branches.en: Shocking excess is the newest and most figurative branch.
branches.cn: 骇人的过分是最新、也最比喻化的一支。

branches.en: Both branches name something good people cannot approve.
branches.cn: 两条义项都指正派人无法认可的事。

branches.en: Both carry a strong sense of what ordinary people find unseemly.
branches.cn: 两条义项都强烈表达「普通人觉得不像话」。

intro.en: Obscene carries no live English prefix or suffix and works only as an adjective, while obscenity and obscenely are built from it.
intro.cn: obscene 不含仍在使用的英语前后缀，只作形容词用；英语围绕它构成 obscenity 与 obscenely。

latinIntro.en: Latin obscenus names bad omens and filth, and the forms obscenitas and obscenus feed the English noun and adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 obscenus 指凶兆与污秽，obscenus 与 obscenitas 分别养出英语的形容词和名词。

items.example: Obscene describes content that shocks.
items.exampleCN: obscene 描述令人震惊的内容。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms obscenity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 obscenity。

items.example: Obscenity is also a legal term.
items.exampleCN: obscenity 也是法律术语。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms obscenely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 obscenely。

items.example: Obscenely often modifies rich or large.
items.exampleCN: obscenely 常修饰「富有、巨大」。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms obsceneness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 obsceneness。

items.example: Obsceneness is rare in modern prose.
items.exampleCN: obsceneness 在现代书面语中很少见。

items.example: Obscenum is the neuter Latin form used for omen.
items.exampleCN: obscenum 是用于表示凶兆的拉丁语中性形式。

items.example: Caenum shaped the modern spelling of obscene.
items.exampleCN: caenum 影响了 obscene 的现代拼写。

items.example: French obscene gave English the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 法语 obscene 给了英语这个形容词。

definition_zh: 晦涩；费解；默默无闻；昏暗；模糊不清的事物
definition_en: the state of being difficult to understand, or of not being well known, or of being dark and hard to see
core_image: 一个人站在浓雾里，只剩模糊的轮廓
scene: 这部老小说引经据典，学生读了三遍还是看不懂其中一段。Students found one passage of the novel surprisingly hard to read because of its obscurity.
sceneCN: 这里 obscurity 是「晦涩、费解」（第 1 个义项：含义难以理解）；句意：学生发现小说中有一段因晦涩难懂而格外难读。

pos.zh: 晦涩；费解；难以理解之处

derivatives.zh: 加 -ity 之前的形容词与动词，义为「晦涩的；使模糊、遮掩」
由 obscure 加 -ly 构成，义为「晦涩地；隐约地」
由 obscurity 的词根加 -antism 构成，义为「蒙昧主义、愚民政策」
指主张或维护蒙昧主义的人或态度

senses.title: Difficulty of understanding
senses.definition: the quality of being hard to understand
senses.definitionCN: 难以理解的性质
senses.example: The obscurity of the legal wording confused many readers.
senses.exampleCN: 法律条文的晦涩让许多读者摸不着头脑。
senses.why: Latin obscurus means covered over, so whatever is hard to understand is a thing whose meaning is shut away from view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obscurus 意为「遮盖起来」，所以难懂的东西就是把含义关在视线之外。

senses.title: The state of being unknown
senses.definition: the state of being little known or of not being noticed
senses.definitionCN: 鲜为人知或不被注意的状态
senses.example: The band rose from obscurity to sell out arenas.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队从默默无闻一跃到场馆座无虚席。
senses.why: If something is covered, nobody can see it, so a person hidden from public view is said to live in obscurity.
senses.whyCN: 东西被盖住就没人看得见，于是不为人了解的人就被说成生活在默默无闻之中。

senses.title: Dimness and indistinctness
senses.definition: the quality of being dark or of being unclear to the senses
senses.definitionCN: 光线黯淡或感官上不清楚的性质
senses.example: The obscurity of the cellar made the steps hard to find.
senses.exampleCN: 地下室昏暗，很难看清台阶。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply not being lit, which the word keeps for dark, blurred things and unclear backgrounds.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是「没有光」，这个词把它保留下来，用于昏暗、模糊的事物和不清楚的来历。

senses.title: An obscure point or detail
senses.definition: a particular point, word, or detail that is hard to follow
senses.definitionCN: 某一个难以理解的论点、词语或细节
senses.example: The essay is full of obscurities that only a specialist can untangle.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章满是只有专家才能理清的晦涩之处。
senses.why: The abstract quality turns into countable pieces, so each murky passage can be called an obscurity.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的性质可以转化为可数的个体，于是每一处含混段落都能称为一个 obscurity。

intro.en: Obscurity comes from Latin obscurus, covered or dark, through the Latin noun obscuritas.
intro.cn: obscurity 来自拉丁语 obscurus（被遮盖的、昏暗的），经拉丁语名词 obscuritas 进入英语。

items.en: Obscurus means dark, covered over, and little known.
items.cn: obscurus 意为昏暗、被遮盖、鲜为人知。

items.en: Obscuritas names darkness and unclear speech.
items.cn: obscuritas 指昏暗与含混不清的言辞。

items.en: Obscurite carries the abstract noun into French.
items.cn: obscurite 把抽象名词带入法语。

items.en: English adopts obscurity first for darkness and unclear meaning.
items.cn: 英语借入 obscurity，先指昏暗与含义不清。

items.en: Writers use it for a lowly or unknown position in life.
items.cn: 作家用它表示低下或不为人的身世处境。

items.en: The word also names the unnoticed life of artists and scientists before fame.
items.cn: 这个词也指艺术家、科学家成名前不为人注意的生活。

note.en: Obscurity belongs to the family of obscure, obscureness, and obscurely, and it sits near vagueness, anonymity, and darkness.
note.cn: obscurity 属于 obscure 词族，与 obscure、obscurely 相邻，在意义上与 vagueness、anonymity、darkness 相邻。

entries.definition: hard to understand or not well known
entries.definitionCN: 晦涩的；鲜为人知的，也是 obscurity 的形容词与动词来源

entries.definition: in a hard or unclear way
entries.definitionCN: 由 obscure 加 -ly 构成的副词，指晦涩地、隐约地

entries.definition: the practice of keeping knowledge from people
entries.definitionCN: 蒙昧主义，与 obscurity 同根，指故意让人知悉不明

entries.definition: the state of being unclear
entries.definitionCN: 模糊；含糊，程度比 obscurity 轻

entries.definition: the state of having an unknown name
entries.definitionCN: 匿名；无名，侧重身份不为人知

entries.definition: a meaning that can be taken in two ways
entries.definitionCN: 歧义；含糊，指有两种理解，而非纯然难懂

normalIntro.en: Obscurity is the noun of being covered over, and it pairs with the verb to fade into obscurity.
normalIntro.cn: obscurity 是表示「被遮盖」的名词，常与 fade into 连用于「被人遗忘」这一说法。

normal.en: The obscurity of the report came from long and tangled sentences.
normal.cn: 这份报告的晦涩来自又长又乱的句子。

normal.en: Many inventors spent years in obscurity before success.
normal.cn: 许多发明家成功前在默默无闻中度过了许多年。

normal.en: Fade into obscurity means slowly being forgotten.
normal.cn: fade into obscurity 表示慢慢被遗忘。

normal.en: The plural obscurities means unclear points.
normal.cn: 复数 obscurities 表示「晦涩之处」。

normal.en: Compare obscene: obscene is about decency, obscurity is about darkness and clearness.
normal.cn: 对比 obscene：obscene 讲体面，obscurity 讲明暗与清晰程度，两者词源不同。

abstract.en: Picture a page whose letters run together in thick fog.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上的字母在浓雾里糊成一片。

abstract.en: Picture a painter with fame arriving only long after death.
abstract.cn: 想象一位在世时无人认识、死后才成名的画家。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp turned down so low that shapes lose their edges.
abstract.cn: 想象灯被调到极暗，物体的轮廓都失去了边界。

examples.en: His poems are read less often now because of their obscurity.
examples.cn: 由于晦涩难懂，他的诗如今读的人少了。

examples.en: The singer lived in obscurity until a video went viral.
examples.cn: 这位歌手一直默默无闻，直到一段视频走红。

examples.en: The cause of the crash remains in obscurity.
examples.cn: 坠机原因至今不明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧不清晰」——「不清晰」就是晦涩、看不清、没人知道，正好对应 obscurity 的意思；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ob-（在前、挡住）+ 与遮盖相关的词根 → obscurus（昏暗的、被遮盖的、难懂的）→ 拉丁语 obscuritas（昏暗；含混）→ 古法语 obscurite → 英语 obscurity，核心义「被遮住、看不见」。

sensesIntro.en: Obscurity begins with darkness, extends to unclear meaning, then to a person or thing hidden from notice, and finally to each murky passage.
sensesIntro.cn: obscurity 从昏暗起步，先指含义不清，再指人或物不为人知，最后指每一处含混的段落。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure barely visible inside thick fog.
core.cn: 核心意象：浓雾中只剩模糊轮廓的人影。

branches.en: Unclear meaning is the main intellectual sense.
branches.cn: 含义不清是主要的思辨义项。

branches.en: Being unknown grows from being unseen.
branches.cn: 不为人知由「看不见」发展而来。

branches.en: Dimness keeps the oldest physical sense.
branches.cn: 昏暗保留了最古老的物理义。

branches.en: Writing that is murky produces countable obscurities.
branches.cn: 含混的文字会制造出一处处晦涩之处。

branches.en: Both faint light and unclear origins keep a thing out of sight.
branches.cn: 不明来历与光线黯淡都是让事物脱离视线。

intro.en: Obscurity is the Latin adjective obscure plus the noun suffix -ity, and the stem also gives obscure, obscurely, and obscurantism.
intro.cn: obscurity 是拉丁形容词 obscure 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，同一词干还生成 obscure、obscurely 与 obscurantism。

latinIntro.en: Latin obscurus means dark or covered, and obscuritas is its abstract noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 obscurus 意为昏暗、被遮盖，obscuritas 是它的抽象名词。

items.example: Obscurus is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: obscurus 是整个词族的根基。

items.example: Obscure keeps the Latin meaning.
items.exampleCN: obscure 保留拉丁语含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms obscurity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 obscurity。

items.example: Obscurity is the abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: obscurity 是抽象名词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms obscurely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 obscurely。

items.example: Obscurely answers the question how.
items.exampleCN: obscurely 回答「怎样地」。

items.example: The suffix -ant feeds the -antism of obscurantism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 参与了 obscurantism 的 -antism 部分。

items.example: Obscurantism blocks the spread of ideas.
items.exampleCN: 蒙昧主义阻碍思想的传播。

items.example: The verb obscure means to make unclear.
items.exampleCN: 动词 obscure 意为使不清楚。

definition_zh: 遵守；奉行；仪式；惯例；（法律、习俗的）遵从
definition_en: the act of obeying a rule, law, or custom, or a ceremony that people keep part of a religion
core_image: 一个人抬头守着规矩，眼睛一直盯着不肯放松
scene: 在清真寺里，信众按传统过节前要先斋戒一个月。Many believers keep the observance of a month of fasting before the festival.
sceneCN: 这里 observance 是「（宗教）仪式、奉行」（第 2 个义项：按传统举行的仪式或惯例）；句意：许多信众在节日之前坚持斋戒一个月的仪式。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ance 之前的动词，义为「遵守；观察；庆祝」
由 observe 加 -ant 构成，义为「遵守的；观察敏锐的」
加前缀 non- 构成，义为「不遵守；违反」

senses.title: The act of obeying a rule
senses.definition: the act of following or obeying a law, rule, or custom
senses.definitionCN: 遵守或奉行法律、规则或习俗的行为
senses.example: The observance of traffic rules saves lives.
senses.exampleCN: 遵守交通规则能救命。
senses.why: The verb observe means to keep watch on something, and keeping watch on a rule became faithfully doing what it says.
senses.whyCN: 动词 observe 意为「注视着」，而一直盯住一条规则，就变成了忠心照做。

senses.title: A customary ceremony
senses.definition: a ceremony or practice that people keep as part of their religion or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 人们作为宗教或传统的一部分保持下来的仪式或做法
senses.example: Many religious observances involve fasting.
senses.exampleCN: 许多宗教仪式都包括斋戒。
senses.why: If you keep watch over a practice and carry it out regularly, the practice itself becomes a named observance.
senses.whyCN: 若你时时守护一种做法并定期去做，这种做法本身就有了 observance 这个名字。

senses.title: Respectful regard
senses.definition: the action of showing respect by following a form or honouring a custom
senses.definitionCN: 通过遵循某种形式或尊重某种习俗来表达敬意
senses.example: Flags flew at half mast in observance of the national day of mourning.
senses.exampleCN: 为纪念全国哀悼日，旗帜降半旗致哀。
senses.why: Because following a rule means respecting it, the word also names public acts of respect done in a set form.
senses.whyCN: 既然遵循规则就是敬重规则，这个词也用于以固定形式公开表达敬意的举动。

intro.en: Observance comes from Latin observare, to keep watch over, from ob in the direction of and servare to watch.
intro.cn: observance 来自拉丁语 observare（守望、注视），由 ob（朝着）与 servare（看守）构成。

items.en: Servare means to watch over or keep safe.
items.cn: servare 意为看守、保全。

items.en: Observare means to pay heed to and to keep to what is prescribed.
items.cn: observare 意为留意、遵守规定。

items.en: Observantia names the act of keeping a rule or a ceremony.
items.cn: observantia 指遵守规则或举行仪式的行为。

items.en: Observance enters French as a learned word for duty and honour.
items.cn: observance 作为书面词进入法语，指职责与敬意。

items.en: English uses observance for keeping religious rules and rites.
items.cn: 英语用 observance 指遵守宗教规则与礼仪。

items.en: The word extends to public memorial ceremonies and to any kept custom.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到公共纪念仪式以及任何沿袭的习俗。

note.en: Observance belongs to the family of observe, observation, and observant, and it stands near compliance, rite, and ceremony.
note.cn: observance 属于 observe 词族，与 observe、observation、observant 相邻，在意义上与 compliance、rite、ceremony 相邻。

entries.definition: to follow a rule or to watch carefully
entries.definitionCN: 遵守；观察，是 observance 去掉名词后缀后得到的动词

entries.definition: quick to notice things or faithful to a rule
entries.definitionCN: 观察敏锐的；遵守教规的，与 observance 同根

entries.definition: the act of watching something closely
entries.definitionCN: 观察；注意，与 observance 同根但侧重「看」而非「守」

entries.definition: the act of obeying a rule or order
entries.definitionCN: 遵从；合规，比 observance 更中性、更偏法律商务

entries.definition: a fixed religious ceremony
entries.definitionCN: 典礼；宗教仪式，侧重仪式本身而非遵守

entries.definition: a formal event held on a special occasion
entries.definitionCN: 典礼；仪式，比 observance 更宏观、更正式

normalIntro.en: Observance keeps the watching image of observe, so it means both watching over a rule and the rite people keep.
normalIntro.cn: observance 保留了 observe 的「注视」意象，所以既指守住规则，也指人们举行的仪式。

normal.en: The verb is observe and the noun is observance, like perform and performance.
normal.cn: 动词是 observe，名词是 observance，构成方式类似 perform 与 performance。

normal.en: In observance of a holiday means as a way of marking that day.
normal.cn: in observance of a holiday 表示「为纪念这个节日」。

normal.en: Religious observance covers prayer, fasting, and holy days.
normal.cn: religious observance 涵盖祈祷、斋戒与圣日。

normal.en: Nonobservance of the rule means breaking it.
normal.cn: nonobservance of the rule 表示不遵守规则。

normal.en: Compare observation: observation means watching, observance means keeping a rule.
normal.cn: 对比 observation：observation 是「看」，observance 是「守」。

abstract.en: Picture a guard who keeps his eyes on the gate all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一名守卫整夜盯着大门。

abstract.en: Picture a family candle lit every year on the same evening.
abstract.cn: 想象一家人每年在同一个晚上点亮同一支蜡烛。

abstract.en: Picture a flag lowered to half mast in a quiet square.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗在安静的广场上缓缓降下半旗。

examples.en: Strict observance of safety rules is required on the site.
examples.cn: 工地上要求严格遵守安全规则。

examples.en: The town holds a yearly observance at the war memorial.
examples.cn: 镇上每年都在战争纪念碑前举行纪念仪式。

examples.en: Some religious observances last for several days.
examples.cn: 有些宗教仪式要持续好几天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额不省的」——规矩「不省」（不能不看清）地守着，就是遵守；仪式上更是步步不省。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ob-（朝着）+ servare（看守）→ observare（留意、遵守）→ 拉丁语 observantia（遵守；敬奉）→ 古法语 observance → 英语 observance，核心义「盯住不放、照章去守」。

sensesIntro.en: Observance grows from watching over a rule, carries that into ceremonies, and finally into public acts of respect.
sensesIntro.cn: observance 从守望规则出发，伸入仪式，最后扩展到公开表达敬意的举动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person keeping watch over a rule without looking away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人目不转睛地守着规矩。

branches.en: Obeying a rule is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 遵守规则是最直白的义项。

branches.en: A kept ceremony is the countable side of the word.
branches.cn: 被保持的仪式是这个词可数的一面。

branches.en: Public respect is the formal and civic branch.
branches.cn: 公开敬意是正式与公共层面的一支。

branches.en: Both keeping a rule and honouring someone are acts of heed.
branches.cn: 遵守规则与致敬他人都是「郑重对待」的行为。

branches.en: A ceremony of respect is often arranged as a set observance.
branches.cn: 表达敬意的仪式常被安排成固定的 observance。

intro.en: Observance is the Latin stem observe plus the noun suffix -ance, and the family includes observe, observation, and observant.
intro.cn: observance 是拉丁词干 observe 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，词族里还有 observe、observation 与 observant。

latinIntro.en: Latin osservare combines ob, toward, with servare, to keep, so observance keeps the idea of guarding a rule.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 observare 由 ob（朝着）与 servare（看守）合成，所以 observance 保留着「守护规则」的意思。

items.example: Servare is the core of the word.
items.exampleCN: servare 是这个词的核心。

items.example: The prefix ob- means in front of or toward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ob- 表示「在前面、朝向」。

items.example: Observare joins watching with keeping a rule.
items.exampleCN: observare 把「看」和「守规则」结合起来。

items.example: Observe keeps both meanings.
items.exampleCN: observe 同时保留两个意思。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ance forms observance.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 构成 observance。

items.meaning: the act of keeping a rule
items.example: Observance names the keeping.
items.exampleCN: observance 指「守」这件事。

items.example: Observation names the watching.
items.exampleCN: observation 指「看」这件事。

items.example: Observant describes the person.
items.exampleCN: observant 描述人。

items.example: The prefix non- forms nonobservance.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 non- 构成 nonobservance。

items.example: Nonobservance is the opposite.
items.exampleCN: nonobservance 是它的反面。

definition_zh: 痴迷；执念；令人着迷的事物
definition_en: a state in which someone thinks about one thing constantly and cannot stop
core_image: 一个人被同一个念头反复拽回，脑子里只有那一件事
scene: 柜台里的球鞋已被人反复看过无数遍，脑海里只剩下那一个念头。For weeks his obsession was a pair of shoes he could not afford.
sceneCN: 这里 obsession 是「痴迷、执念」（第 1 个义项：心里被同一件事长期占据、无法摆脱）；句意：有好几周，他痴迷的就是一双买不起的球鞋。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀构成，义为「使着迷；使心神不宁」
obsession 加 -ive 构成，义为「着迷的；强迫性的」
obsessive 加 -ly 构成，义为「着迷地；执拗地」
obsession 加 -al 构成，义为「与执念有关的；强迫性的」

senses.title: A thought that will not let go
senses.definition: a persistent thought or feeling that keeps returning and cannot easily be dismissed
senses.definitionCN: 反复出现、难以摆脱的一个念头或情绪
senses.example: His obsession with the past stopped him from moving on.
senses.exampleCN: 他对过去的执念让他无法向前走。
senses.why: The Latin prefix ob- adds a sense of against or towards, and the root sid- means to sit, so the picture is a thought sitting down on the mind and refusing to leave.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 ob- 带来「朝向、对着」的意味，词根 sid- 意为坐，所以画面是一个念头坐在心上赖着不走，这就是执念。

senses.title: To be occupied by one thought
senses.definition: the state of thinking about one thing so much that other things are pushed aside
senses.definitionCN: 过度想着某一件事，以致把其他事情都推到一边的状态
senses.example: Her sudden obsession with fitness surprised her friends.
senses.exampleCN: 她突然迷上健身，这让朋友们很意外。
senses.why: Once the thought keeps sitting there, attention is captured by it, so the word also names the state of being absorbed or hooked.
senses.whyCN: 念头一旦长期占据，注意力就被它抓走，于是这个词也指被某事牢牢吸住、着迷的状态。

senses.title: The thing that grips the mind
senses.definition: something that a person cannot stop thinking about or wanting
senses.definitionCN: 令人无法停止想着或渴望的事物
senses.example: Football is a national obsession in that country.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个国家，足球是全民痴迷的事。
senses.why: The mental state is transferred to the object that causes it, so a hobby or hobbyhorse is called an obsession.
senses.whyCN: 心理状态被转移到引起它的对象上，所以某件爱好或某个话题也可以叫 obsession，即「让人着迷的事」。

intro.en: Obsession comes from Latin obsidere, to sit down before or besiege, built on ob- and sedere, to sit.
intro.cn: obsession 来自拉丁语 obsidere（坐到前面、围困），由 ob- 与 sedere（坐）构成。

items.en: Sedere means to sit, and ob- adds before, against, or towards.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐，ob- 表示在前、对着或朝向。

items.en: Obses means a blockade, and obsidere means to besiege a place.
items.cn: obses 意为围困，obsidere 意为围攻某地。

items.en: In early medical Latin, obsessio names a siege of the mind by an evil spirit.
items.cn: 十六世纪医学拉丁语中，obsessio 指邪灵对心灵的侵袭。

items.en: Obsession passes into French, where it first means the action of besieging.
items.cn: obsession 进入法语，最初表示围攻这一行为。

items.en: English obsession still carries a military and demonic flavour.
items.cn: 英语中的 obsession 仍带有军事与邪灵侵袭的色彩。

items.en: Nineteenth and twentieth century psychiatry turns it into an idea that takes hold of the mind.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪的精神医学把它变成抓住大脑不放的念头。

note.en: Obsession belongs to the family of obsess, obsessive, and obsessively, and sits beside milder words for strong interest.
note.cn: obsession 与 obsess、obsessive、obsessively 同属一个词族，并与表示强烈兴趣的若干词相邻。

normalIntro.cn: obsession 的画面是一个念头「坐」进脑子里：来自拉丁语 ob- 加 sedere（坐）。

normal.en: obsession with money means an unhealthy hunger for it.
